version, pointwise at `u`: `∂̄_I (g ∘ f) = deriv g (f u) · ∂̄_I f`. As in
`dWirtingerCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply`, the `∂g/∂f̄` channel vanishes and `∂g/∂f`
collapses to `deriv g (f u)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_holomorphic_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g (f u)) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => g (f v)) I u =
      deriv g (f u) * dWirtingerAntiCoord f I u

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_star_comp_apply
declarations.doc:
Conjugating the inner field swaps the two operators: `∂̄_I f̄ = conj (∂_I f)`. Dual of
`dWirtingerCoord_star_comp_apply`, the `d = Pi.single I 1` case of the foundation
`dWirtingerAntiDir_star_comp`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_star_comp_apply {u : (ι → ℂ)}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f u) (I : ι) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v : (ι → ℂ) => star (f v)) I u =
      star (dWirtingerCoord f I u)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerCoord
declarations.doc:
On a `C²` function the holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative is itself
real-differentiable (`DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂_I f) u`) — the `d = Pi.single I 1` case of
`differentiableAt_dWirtingerDir`.
declarations.statement:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerCoord (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (I : ι) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun v => dWirtingerCoord f I v) u

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiCoord
declarations.doc:
On a `C²` function the anti-holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative is itself
real-differentiable (`DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂̄_J f) u`) — the `d = Pi.single J 1` case of
`differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiDir`.
declarations.statement:
lemma differentiableAt_dWirtingerAntiCoord (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (J : ι) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun v => dWirtingerAntiCoord f J v) u

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_dWirtingerAntiCoord_comm
declarations.doc:
**Schwarz's theorem** for the coordinate Wirtinger operators: on a `C²` function the
holomorphic and anti-holomorphic derivatives commute, `∂_I ∂̄_J f = ∂̄_J ∂_I f`. The
`d = Pi.single I 1`, `e = Pi.single J 1` case of the general
`dWirtingerDir_dWirtingerAntiDir_comm`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dWirtingerCoord_dWirtingerAntiCoord_comm (hf2 : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f u) (I J : ι) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => dWirtingerAntiCoord f J v) I u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => dWirtingerCoord f I v) J u

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero
declarations.doc:
If the inner continuous ℝ-linear map `P` kills the coordinate column `c`, the holomorphic
coordinate Wirtinger derivative of `h ∘ P` along `c` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (u : D → ℂ)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = 0) (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = 0) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col
declarations.doc:
If the inner continuous ℝ-linear map `P` reads the coordinate column `c` as the sector
coordinate `a₀`, the holomorphic coordinate Wirtinger derivative of `h ∘ P` along `c` is that
of `h` along `a₀`, evaluated at `P u`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s] [DecidableEq C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (a₀ : C_s)
    (u : D → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = Pi.single a₀ 1)
    (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = Pi.single a₀ Complex.I) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = dWirtingerCoord h a₀ (P u)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_zero
declarations.doc: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_zero`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_zero {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (u : D → ℂ)
    (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = 0) (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = 0) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_col
declarations.doc: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_comp_clm_col`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_comp_clm_col {C_s : Type} [Fintype C_s] [DecidableEq C_s]
    (P : (D → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (C_s → ℂ)) (h : (C_s → ℂ) → ℂ) (c : D) (a₀ : C_s)
    (u : D → ℂ) (hh : DifferentiableAt ℝ h (P u))
    (h1 : P (Pi.single c 1) = Pi.single a₀ 1)
    (hI : P (Pi.single c Complex.I) = Pi.single a₀ Complex.I) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun v => h (P v)) c u = dWirtingerAntiCoord h a₀ (P u)

modules.title: The mixed Wirtinger Hessian
modules.doc:
The mixed Wirtinger Hessian, and its block-diagonal form for a sum of sector functions.

## i. Overview

In an `N = 1` supersymmetric theory the kinetic terms of the complex scalar fields `φ^I` are
weighted by the Kähler metric

  `g_{IJ̄}(φ) = ∂_I ∂̄_J K(φ)`,   `∂_I = ∂/∂φ^I`,   `∂̄_J = ∂/∂φ̄^J`,

of the real Kähler potential `K`. The metric is Hermitian, `(g_{JĪ})^* = g_{IJ̄}`, so the kinetic
term is real.

Suppose the fields split into sectors `k`, with fields `φ_k = (φ_k^a)` in sector `k`, and the
Kähler potential is a sum of sector potentials with no term mixing two sectors:

  `K(φ) = ∑_k K_k(φ_k)`,

as for several moduli `T_k` with `K = -∑_k n_k log(T_k + T̄_k)` and positive constants `n_k`.
Then the metric is block-diagonal and the sectors have no kinetic mixing:

  `∂²K / ∂φ_k^a ∂φ̄_l^b = δ_{kl} ∂²K_k / ∂φ_k^a ∂φ̄_k^b`.

Each `K_k` need only be `C²` at the point considered, so potentials defined on a proper
subdomain, such as `log`, are covered.

In Lean, the fields of sector `k` are labelled by a finite type `ι k`, and the field `φ_k^a`
by the pair `⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k`. A point `φ` in field space is a function
`q : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ` with `q ⟨k, a⟩ = φ_k^a`, and the sector fields `φ_k` are
`q ∘ Sigma.mk k`, the function `a ↦ q ⟨k, a⟩`. The sector potentials `K_k` are `f k`. The
metric `g_{IJ̄}(φ)` is `hessianMatrixOfR K q`, or `hessianMatrixOf` for a complex-valued
function. At a point `u`, the block-diagonal statement reads

  `hessianMatrixOf (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) u`
  `  = blockDiagonal' (fun k => hessianMatrixOf (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k))`.

The two-sector case over `ι₁ ⊕ ι₂` is stated with `Matrix.fromBlocks`.

## ii. Key results

- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf` : the mixed Wirtinger Hessian.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR` : the same for a real-valued function.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR_isHermitian` : the Hessian of a real `C²` function is
    Hermitian.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_sum` : `∂̄` of a sum of sector functions along a
    sector-`k` coordinate is the `∂̄` of the sector-`k` function; `dWirtingerCoord_block_sum` is
    the same for `∂`.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_sum_eq_blockDiagonal'` : the Hessian of a sum of sector
    functions is block-diagonal.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_comp_equiv` : relabelling the coordinates by `ε` reindexes
    the Hessian by `ε`.
- `Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_add_eq_fromBlocks` : the two-sector case, as
    `Matrix.fromBlocks`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mixed Wirtinger Hessian
- B. Block-diagonal Hessian of a sum over sectors
- C. Coordinate reindexing of the Hessian
- D. Two sectors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The mixed Wirtinger Hessian

For a real Kähler potential `K` the mixed Wirtinger Hessian is the Kähler metric `g_{IJ̄}`.
Reality of `K` and Schwarz's theorem make it Hermitian.

## B. Block-diagonal Hessian of a sum over sectors

The fields are labelled by `Σ k, ι k`, with `ι k` labelling the fields of sector `k`. A potential
that is a sum of sector potentials has a block-diagonal Hessian.

## C. Coordinate reindexing of the Hessian

Relabelling the fields by a bijection `ε` permutes the rows and columns of the Hessian.

## D. Two sectors

Two sectors with fields indexed by `ι₁ ⊕ ι₂`, obtained from §B by relabelling with §C.

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf
declarations.doc: The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of `f` at `u`: the matrix with `(I, J)` entry `∂_I ∂̄_J f`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hessianMatrixOf (f : (ι → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι → ℂ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR
declarations.doc:
The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of a real-valued `K`, through `Complex.ofReal`. An `abbrev`, so
lemmas about `hessianMatrixOf` apply to it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev hessianMatrixOfR (K : (ι → ℂ) → ℝ) (u : ι → ℂ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOfR_isHermitian
declarations.doc:
The mixed Wirtinger Hessian of a real function `C²` at `u` is Hermitian,
`(g_{JĪ})^* = g_{IJ̄}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hessianMatrixOfR_isHermitian {K : (ι → ℂ) → ℝ} {u : ι → ℂ} (hK : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 K u) :
    Matrix.IsHermitian (hessianMatrixOfR K u)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict
declarations.doc: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sigma.mk k` to sector `k`, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def restrict (k : K) : ((Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι k → ℂ)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict_apply
declarations.statement: lemma restrict_apply (k : K) (q : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) : restrict k q = q ∘ Sigma.mk k

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict_single_same
declarations.doc: `restrict k` sends the basis vector of field `⟨k, a'⟩` to the basis vector of field `a'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_single_same (k : K) (a' : ι k) (z : ℂ) :
    restrict k (Pi.single (⟨k, a'⟩ : Σ k, ι k) z) = Pi.single a' z

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrict_single_ne
declarations.doc: `restrict k` sends the basis vector of a field of another sector to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_single_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (a' : ι k') (z : ℂ) :
    restrict k (Pi.single (⟨k', a'⟩ : Σ k, ι k) z) = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_own
declarations.doc: `∂_⟨k, a⟩` of a function of sector `k` alone is its `∂_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_own {k : K} (g : (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u
      = dWirtingerCoord g a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_ne
declarations.doc: `∂_⟨k, a⟩` of a function of another sector vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (g : (ι k' → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k')) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k')) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_own
declarations.doc: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_block_own`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_own {k : K} (g : (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord g a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_ne
declarations.doc: Anti-holomorphic mirror of `dWirtingerCoord_block_ne`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_ne {k k' : K} (h : k ≠ k') (g : (ι k' → ℂ) → ℂ) (a : ι k)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (u ∘ Sigma.mk k')) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => g (q ∘ Sigma.mk k')) (⟨k, a⟩ : Σ k, ι k) u = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerCoord_block_sum
declarations.doc: `∂_⟨k₀, a⟩` of a sum of sector functions is the `∂_a` of the sector-`k₀` function.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerCoord_block_sum (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (k₀ : K) (a : ι k₀)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hf : ∀ k, DifferentiableAt ℝ (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerCoord (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) ⟨k₀, a⟩ u
      = dWirtingerCoord (f k₀) a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k₀)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_sum
declarations.doc: `∂̄_⟨k₀, a⟩` of a sum of sector functions is the `∂̄_a` of the sector-`k₀` function.
declarations.statement:
lemma dWirtingerAntiCoord_block_sum (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (k₀ : K) (a : ι k₀)
    (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ) (hf : ∀ k, DifferentiableAt ℝ (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    dWirtingerAntiCoord (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) ⟨k₀, a⟩ u
      = dWirtingerAntiCoord (f k₀) a (u ∘ Sigma.mk k₀)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_sum_eq_blockDiagonal'
declarations.doc:
The Hessian of a sum of sector functions is the block-diagonal matrix of the sector
Hessians.
declarations.statement:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_sum_eq_blockDiagonal' (f : ∀ k, (ι k → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : (Σ k, ι k) → ℂ)
    (hf : ∀ k, ContDiffAt ℝ 2 (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => ∑ k, f k (q ∘ Sigma.mk k)) u
      = blockDiagonal' (fun k => hessianMatrixOf (f k) (u ∘ Sigma.mk k))

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.precompEquiv
declarations.doc: The relabelling `q ↦ q ∘ ε.symm` along `ε`, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def precompEquiv (ε : ι ≃ ι') : (ι → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι' → ℂ)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.precompEquiv_single
declarations.doc: `precompEquiv ε` sends the basis vector of field `c` to the basis vector of field `ε c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma precompEquiv_single (ε : ι ≃ ι') (c : ι) (z : ℂ) :
    precompEquiv ε (Pi.single c z) = Pi.single (ε c) z

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_comp_equiv
declarations.doc: Relabelling the coordinates by `ε` reindexes the Hessian by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_comp_equiv (ε : ι ≃ ι') (H : (ι' → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι → ℂ)
    (hH : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 H (u ∘ ε.symm)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => H (q ∘ ε.symm)) u
      = (hessianMatrixOf H (u ∘ ε.symm)).submatrix ε ε

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInl
declarations.doc: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sum.inl` to the first sector, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def restrictInl : (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι₁ → ℂ)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInr
declarations.doc: The restriction `q ↦ q ∘ Sum.inr` to the second sector, as a continuous ℝ-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def restrictInr : (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) →L[ℝ] (ι₂ → ℂ)

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInl_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictInl_apply (q : ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) :
    restrictInl (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) q = q ∘ Sum.inl

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.restrictInr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrictInr_apply (q : ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ) :
    restrictInr (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) q = q ∘ Sum.inr

declarations.name: Physlib.Wirtinger.hessianMatrixOf_add_eq_fromBlocks
declarations.doc:
The Hessian of `f₁ (q ∘ Sum.inl) + f₂ (q ∘ Sum.inr)` is `fromBlocks` of the two sector
Hessians.
declarations.statement:
lemma hessianMatrixOf_add_eq_fromBlocks
    (f₁ : (ι₁ → ℂ) → ℂ) (f₂ : (ι₂ → ℂ) → ℂ) (u : ι₁ ⊕ ι₂ → ℂ)
    (hf₁ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f₁ (u ∘ Sum.inl)) (hf₂ : ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f₂ (u ∘ Sum.inr)) :
    hessianMatrixOf (fun q => f₁ (q ∘ Sum.inl) + f₂ (q ∘ Sum.inr)) u
      = Matrix.fromBlocks (hessianMatrixOf f₁ (u ∘ Sum.inl)) 0 0
          (hessianMatrixOf f₂ (u ∘ Sum.inr))

modules.doc:
## The multiple of a Schwartz map by `x`

In this module we define the continuous linear map from the Schwartz space
`𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)` to itself which takes a Schwartz map `η` to the Schwartz map `x * η`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.norm_iteratedFDeriv_ofRealCLM
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_iteratedFDeriv_ofRealCLM {x} (i : ℕ) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i (RCLike.ofRealCLM (K := 𝕜)) x‖ =
      if i = 0 then |x| else if i = 1 then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.powOneMul
declarations.doc:
The continuous linear map `𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)` taking a Schwartz map
`η` to `x * η`.
declarations.statement: def powOneMul : 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.powOneMul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma powOneMul_apply (ψ : 𝓢(ℝ, 𝕜)) (x : ℝ) :
    powOneMul 𝕜 ψ x = x * ψ x

modules.title: Distributions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Distributions are often used implicitly in physics, for example the correct way to handle
a dirac delta function is to treat it as a distribution. In this file we will
define distributions and some properties on them.

The distributions from a space `E` to space `F` can be thought of as a generalization of
functions from `E` to `F`. We give a more precise definition of distributions below.

In this file we define distributions generally. Properties of distributions directly related to
`Space` are defined in the `Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space` directory, for example in
`Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space.DistOfFunction`.

## ii. Key results

- `E →d[𝕜] F` is the type of distributions from `E` to `F`.
- `Distribution.derivative` and `Distribution.fourierTransform` allow us to make sense of these
  operations that might not make sense a priori on general functions.
- `Distribution.toTemperedDistribution` converts a Physlib distribution to a Mathlib
  tempered distribution.
- `Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure` is the scalar distribution associated to a finite measure.
- `Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure_eq_iff` says that finite measures are determined by their
  associated complex scalar distributions.
- `Distribution.integralOfBound` integrates a family with an integrable Schwartz seminorm bound.
- `Distribution.fderivD_integralOfBound_apply` differentiates this integral after evaluation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of a distribution
- B. Construction of distributions from linear maps
- C. Derivatives of distributions
  - C.1. Differentiating integrals of distributions
- D. Fourier transform of distributions
  - D.1. Bridge to Mathlib tempered distributions
- E. Specific distributions
  - E.1. The constant distribution
  - E.2. Distributions associated to finite measures
  - E.3. The dirac delta distribution
  - E.4. The heaviside step function

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The definition of a distribution

In physics, we often encounter mathematical objects like the Dirac delta function `δ(x)`
that are not functions in the traditional sense.
Distributions provide a rigorous framework for handling such objects.

The core idea is to define a "generalized function" not by its value at each point,
but by how it acts on a set of well-behaved "test functions".

These test functions, typically denoted `η`. The choice of test functions depends on the application
here we choose test functions which are smooth and decay
rapidly at infinity (called Schwartz maps). Thus really the distributions we are defining here
are called tempered distributions.

A distribution `u` is a linear map that takes a test function `η` and produces a value,
which can be a scalar or a vector. This action is written as `⟪u,η⟫`.

Two key examples illustrate this concept:

1. **Ordinary Functions:** Any well-behaved function `f(x)` can be viewed as a distribution.
  Its action on a test function `η` is defined by integration:
  `u_f(η) = ∫ f(x) η(x) dx`
  This integral "tests" the function `f` using `η`.

2. **Dirac Delta:** The Dirac delta `δ_a` (centered at `a`) is a distribution whose action is to
  simply evaluate the test function at `a`:
  `δ_a(η) = η(a)`

Formally, a distribution is a *continuous linear map* from the space of Schwartz functions
`𝓢(E, 𝕜)` to a
vector space `F` over `𝕜`. This definition allows us to rigorously define concepts
like derivatives and Fourier transforms for these generalized functions, as we will see below.

We use the notation `E →d[𝕜] F` to denote the space of distributions from `E` to `F`
where `E` is a normed vector space over `ℝ` and `F` is a normed vector space over `𝕜`.

## B. Construction of distributions from linear maps

Distributions are defined as **continuous** linear maps from `𝓢(E, 𝕜)` to `F`.
It is possible to define a constructor of distributions from just linear maps
`𝓢(E, 𝕜) →ₗ[𝕜] F` (without the continuity requirement) by imposing a condition
on the size of `u` applied to `η`.

## C. Derivatives of distributions

Given a distribution `u : E →d[𝕜] F`, we can define the derivative of that distribution.
In general when defining an operation on a distribution, we do it by applying a similar
operation instead to the Schwartz maps it acts on.

Thus the derivative of `u` is the distribution which takes `η` to `⟪u, - η'⟫`
where `η'` is the derivative of `η`.

The derivative commutes with finite superpositions of sources: for a family `u` and a finite
index set `s`, the identity `fderivD 𝕜 (∑ i ∈ s, u i) = ∑ i ∈ s, fderivD 𝕜 (u i)` follows from
`map_sum (fderivD 𝕜) u s`, since `fderivD 𝕜` is a linear map. Integrals of families of
distributions are treated in the next subsection.

### C.1. Differentiating integrals of distributions

Superpositions of generalized sources can be described by integrating families of distributions.
We construct this weak integral when evaluations are measurable and bounded by an integrable
coefficient times a fixed finite maximum of Schwartz seminorms. This bound ensures that the
integral is continuous on the test functions. Distributional differentiation then commutes with
the integral after evaluation at a test function and a direction.

## D. Fourier transform of distributions

As with derivatives of distributions we can define the fourier transform of a distribution
by taking the fourier transform of the underlying Schwartz maps. Thus the fourier transform
of the distribution `u` is the distribution which takes `η` to `⟪u, F[η]⟫` where `F[η]` is the
fourier transform of `η`.

### D.1. Bridge to Mathlib tempered distributions

Mathlib's tempered distributions use the pointwise convergence topology on the same underlying
continuous linear maps. The following construction converts Physlib distributions to that API.

## E. Specific distributions

We now define specific distributions, which are used throughout physics. In particular, we define:
- The constant distribution.
- Distributions associated to finite measures.
- The dirac delta distribution.
- The heaviside step function.

### E.1. The constant distribution

The constant distribution is the distribution which corresponds to a constant function,
it takes `η` to the integral of `η` over the volume measure.

### E.2. Distributions associated to finite measures

Every finite measure has temperate growth, so integrating Schwartz maps against it defines a
scalar distribution.

### E.3. The dirac delta distribution

The dirac delta distribution centered at `a : E` is the distribution which takes
`η` to `η a`. We also define `diracDelta'` which takes in an element of `v` of `F` and
outputs `η a • v`.

### E.4. The heaviside step function

The heaviside step function on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ)` is the distribution
from `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ)` to `ℝ` which takes a `η` to the integral of `η` in the
upper-half plane (determined by the last coordinate in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ)`).

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution
declarations.doc:
An `F`-valued distribution on `E` (where `E` is a normed vector space over `ℝ` and `F` is a
normed vector space over `𝕜`) is a continuous linear map `𝓢(E, 𝕜) →L[𝕜] F` where `𝒮(E, 𝕜)` is
the Schwartz space of smooth functions `E → 𝕜` with rapidly decreasing iterated derivatives. This
is notated as `E →d[𝕜] F`.

This should be seen as a generalisation of functions `E → F`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Distribution (𝕜 E F : Type) [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] : Type

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofLinear
declarations.doc:
The construction of a distribution from the following data:
1. We take a finite set `s` of pairs `(k, n) ∈ ℕ × ℕ` that will be explained later.
2. We take a linear map `u` that evaluates the given Schwartz function `η`. At this stage we don't
  need `u` to be continuous.
3. Recall that a Schwartz function `η` satisfies a bound
  `‖x‖ᵏ * ‖(dⁿ/dxⁿ) η‖ < Mₙₖ` where `Mₙₖ : ℝ` only depends on `(k, n) : ℕ × ℕ`.
4. This step is where `s` is used: for each test function `η`, the norm `‖u η‖` is required to be
  bounded by `C * (‖x‖ᵏ * ‖(dⁿ/dxⁿ) η‖)` for some `x : ℝ` and for some `(k, n) ∈ s`, where
  `C ≥ 0` is a global scalar.

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofLinear_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofLinear_apply (s : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (u : 𝓢(E, 𝕜) →ₗ[𝕜] F)
    (hu : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜), ∃ (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (x : E), (k, n) ∈ s ∧
      ‖u η‖ ≤ C * (‖x‖ ^ k * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η x‖))
    (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    ofLinear 𝕜 s u hu η = u η

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fderivD
declarations.doc:
The Fréchet derivative of a distribution.

Informally, for a distribution `u : E →d[𝕜] F`,
the Fréchet derivative `fderiv u x v` corresponds to the derivative of `u` at the
point `x` in the direction `v`. For example, if `F = ℝ³`
then `fderiv u x v` is a vector in `ℝ³` corresponding to
`(v₁ ∂u₁/∂x₁ + v₂ ∂u₁/∂x₂ + v₃ ∂u₁/∂x₃, v₁ ∂u₂/∂x₁ + v₂ ∂u₂/∂x₂ + v₃ ∂u₂/∂x₃,...)`.

Formally, for a distribution `u : E →d[𝕜] F`, this is actually defined
the distribution which takes test function `η : E → 𝕜` to
`- u (SchwartzMap.evalCLM v (SchwartzMap.fderivCLM 𝕜 η))`.

Note that, unlike for functions, the Fréchet derivative of a distribution always exists.
declarations.statement: def fderivD [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] : (E →d[𝕜] F) →ₗ[𝕜] (E →d[𝕜] (E →L[ℝ] F))

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fderivD_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderivD_apply [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (u : E →d[𝕜] F) (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) (v : E) :
    fderivD 𝕜 u η v = - u (SchwartzMap.evalCLM (𝕜 := 𝕜) E 𝕜 v (SchwartzMap.fderivCLM 𝕜 E 𝕜 η))

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.integrable_eval_of_bound
declarations.doc: Evaluations of a distribution family with an integrable seminorm bound are integrable.
declarations.statement: lemma integrable_eval_of_bound (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) : Integrable (fun a => u a η) μ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.integralOfBound
declarations.doc:
The weak integral of a family of distributions with an integrable Schwartz seminorm bound.
It acts on a test function by integrating the evaluations of the family.
declarations.statement: def integralOfBound : E →d[𝕜] F

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.integralOfBound_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the weak integral is the integral of the evaluations.
declarations.statement:
lemma integralOfBound_apply (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    integralOfBound u s b hb hmeas hbound hb_nonneg η = ∫ a, u a η ∂μ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.integrable_fderivD_eval_of_bound
declarations.doc: Differentiated evaluations of a family with an integrable seminorm bound are integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_fderivD_eval_of_bound (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) (v : E) :
    Integrable (fun a => fderivD 𝕜 (u a) η v) μ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fderivD_integralOfBound_apply
declarations.doc:
Distributional differentiation commutes with the weak integral after evaluation at a test
function and a direction.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderivD_integralOfBound_apply (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) (v : E) :
    fderivD 𝕜 (integralOfBound u s b hb hmeas hbound hb_nonneg) η v =
      ∫ a, fderivD 𝕜 (u a) η v ∂μ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fourierTransform
declarations.doc:
Definition of Fourier transform of distribution: Let `u` be a distribution. Then its Fourier
transform is `F{u}` where given a test function `η`, `F{u}(η) := u(F{η})`.
declarations.statement: def fourierTransform : (E →d[ℂ] F) →ₗ[ℂ] (E →d[ℂ] F)

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fourierTransform_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierTransform_apply (u : E →d[ℂ] F) (η : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    u.fourierTransform E F η = u (fourierTransformCLM ℂ η)

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution
declarations.doc: The Mathlib tempered distribution associated to a Physlib distribution.
declarations.statement: def toTemperedDistribution (u : E →d[ℂ] F) : 𝓢'(E, F)

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma toTemperedDistribution_apply (u : E →d[ℂ] F) (η : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) :
    u.toTemperedDistribution η = u η

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution_fourierTransform
declarations.doc: Conversion to Mathlib tempered distributions commutes with the Fourier transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma toTemperedDistribution_fourierTransform (u : E →d[ℂ] F) :
    (u.fourierTransform E F).toTemperedDistribution = 𝓕 u.toTemperedDistribution

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.const
declarations.doc:
The constant distribution `E →d[𝕜] F`, for a given `c : F` this corresponds
to the integral `∫ x, η x • c ∂MeasureTheory.volume`.
declarations.statement: def const [hμ : Measure.HasTemperateGrowth (volume (α := E))] (c : F) : E →d[𝕜] F

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.const_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma const_apply [hμ : Measure.HasTemperateGrowth (volume (α := E))] (c : F)
    (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    const 𝕜 E c η = ∫ x, η x • c ∂MeasureTheory.volume

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.fderivD_const
declarations.statement:
lemma fderivD_const [hμ : Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure (volume (α := E))]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (c : F) :
    fderivD ℝ (const ℝ E c) = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure
declarations.doc:
The scalar distribution associated to a finite measure, acting on a Schwartz map by
integration.
declarations.statement: def ofFiniteMeasure (μ : Measure E) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] : E →d[𝕜] 𝕜

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFiniteMeasure_apply (μ : Measure E) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    ofFiniteMeasure 𝕜 μ η = ∫ x, η x ∂μ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.toTemperedDistribution_ofFiniteMeasure
declarations.doc:
The finite-measure distribution agrees with Mathlib's tempered distribution associated to the
same measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma toTemperedDistribution_ofFiniteMeasure (μ : Measure E) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] :
    (ofFiniteMeasure ℂ μ).toTemperedDistribution = μ.toTemperedDistribution

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.ofFiniteMeasure_eq_iff
declarations.doc: The complex scalar distribution associated to a finite measure determines the measure.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFiniteMeasure_eq_iff
    {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E]
    [BorelSpace E] [SecondCountableTopology E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    {μ ν : Measure E} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] :
    ofFiniteMeasure ℂ μ = ofFiniteMeasure ℂ ν ↔ μ = ν

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.diracDelta
declarations.doc:
Dirac delta distribution `diracDelta 𝕜 a : E →d[𝕜] 𝕜` takes in a test function `η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)`
and outputs `η a`. Intuitively this is an infinite density at a single point `a`.
declarations.statement: def diracDelta (a : E) : E →d[𝕜] 𝕜

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.diracDelta_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma diracDelta_apply (a : E) (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    diracDelta 𝕜 a η = η a

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.diracDelta'
declarations.doc:
Dirac delta in a given direction `v : F`. `diracDelta' 𝕜 a v` takes in a test function
`η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)` and outputs `η a • v`. Intuitively this is an infinitely intense vector field
at a single point `a` pointing at the direction `v`.
declarations.statement: def diracDelta' (a : E) (v : F) : E →d[𝕜] F

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.diracDelta'_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma diracDelta'_apply (a : E) (v : F) (η : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)) :
    diracDelta' 𝕜 a v η = η a • v

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.heavisideStep
declarations.doc:
The Heaviside step distribution defined on `(EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ)) `
equal to `1` in the positive `z`-direction and `0` in the negative `z`-direction.
declarations.statement: def heavisideStep (d : ℕ) : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ)) →d[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: Physlib.Distribution.heavisideStep_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma heavisideStep_apply (d : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ), ℝ)) :
    heavisideStep d η = ∫ x in {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d.succ) | 0 < x (Fin.last d)},
      η x ∂MeasureTheory.volume

modules.title: Upgrading a real-linear map to a complex-linear one
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

An `ℝ`-linear map between complex vector spaces that commutes with multiplication by `i` is
`ℂ`-linear, since `c = c.re + c.im · i`. Mathlib has the case of a map out of `ℂ`
(`real_linearMap_map_smul_complex`, `ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfReal`); this file treats an
arbitrary domain.

## ii. Key results

- `LinearMap.map_smul_of_commutesI` : the law along one direction.
- `LinearMap.commutesI_of_basis` : commuting with `i` on a `ℂ`-basis suffices.
- `ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfCommutesI` : the resulting continuous `ℂ`-linear map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scalar law
- B. Commuting with `i` on a basis
- C. The complex-linear map

## iv. References

There are no known references for the material in this module.

sections.text: ## A. The scalar law
## B. Commuting with `i` on a basis
## C. The complex-linear map

declarations.name: LinearMap.map_smul_of_commutesI
declarations.doc: An `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i` along `v` commutes with every complex scalar along `v`.

declarations.name: LinearMap.commutesI_of_basis
declarations.doc: An `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i` on a `ℂ`-basis commutes with `i` everywhere.
declarations.statement:
lemma commutesI_of_basis {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (L : V →ₗ[ℝ] E) (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V)
    (h : ∀ i, L (Complex.I • b i) = Complex.I • L (b i)) (v : V) :
    L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfCommutesI
declarations.doc: A continuous `ℝ`-linear map commuting with `i`, as a continuous `ℂ`-linear map.
declarations.statement:
def complexOfCommutesI (L : V →L[ℝ] E)
    (h : ∀ v, L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v) : V →L[ℂ] E

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.complexOfCommutesI_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma complexOfCommutesI_apply (L : V →L[ℝ] E)
    (h : ∀ v, L (Complex.I • v) = Complex.I • L v) (v : V) :
    complexOfCommutesI L h v = L v

modules.title: The coordinate pairing of two bases
modules.doc:
Two bases with the same labels pair two modules by their coordinates.

## i. Overview

Mathlib pairs a module `M` with its own dual. In physics the space paired with `M` is often a
type of its own with its own basis, not `Module.Dual M`. Covectors `w_μ`, with the basis `e^μ`,
pair with vectors `x^μ`, with the basis `e_μ`, as `x^μ w_μ = ∑ μ, x^μ w_μ`. This file gives that
pairing for any two modules `M` and `N` with bases `b` and `b'` labelled by the same finite type
`ι`, and shows that it identifies `N` with the dual of `M`, so Mathlib's results on duals apply.

The coordinate pairing `coordPairing` sends `x ⊗ y` to `∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`. It is Mathlib's
`b'.toDual`, applied after the equivalence `b.equiv b'` that sends `b I` to `b' I`. The two bases
are dual for it, it is the only pairing for which they are, and it is a perfect pairing in
Mathlib's sense. When the two modules carry representations and some invariant pairing makes the
bases dual, the coordinate pairing is that pairing, so it is invariant.

## ii. Key results

- `Module.Basis.coordPairing` : the coordinate pairing `∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I` of two bases with
  the same labels.
- `Module.Basis.coordPairing_basis_basis` : the two bases are dual for the coordinate pairing, and
  `Module.Basis.eq_coordPairing` : it is the only such pairing.
- `Module.Basis.isPerfPair_coordPairing` : the coordinate pairing is a perfect pairing.
- `Module.Basis.coordPairing_invariant` : the coordinate pairing is invariant when an invariant
  pairing makes the bases dual.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The coordinate pairing of two bases
- B. Invariance of the coordinate pairing

## iv. References

There are no known references for the material in this module.

sections.text: ## A. The coordinate pairing of two bases
## B. Invariance of the coordinate pairing

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing
declarations.doc:
The coordinate pairing `M ⊗ N → R` of two bases with the same labels. It sends `x ⊗ y` to
`b'.toDual x' y`, where `x'` is the vector of `N` with the coordinates of `x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coordPairing (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) :
    M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[R] R

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing_tmul_basis
declarations.doc: Pairing with the second basis reads off a coordinate, `b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ b' J) = x_J`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coordPairing_tmul_basis (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) (x : M) (J : ι) :
    b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ[R] b' J) = b.equivFun x J

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing_tmul
declarations.doc: `b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coordPairing_tmul (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) = ∑ I, b.equivFun x I * b'.equivFun y I

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing_basis_basis
declarations.doc: The two bases are dual, `b.coordPairing b' (b I ⊗ₜ b' J) = δ_{IJ}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coordPairing_basis_basis (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) (I J : ι) :
    b.coordPairing b' (b I ⊗ₜ[R] b' J) = if I = J then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Module.Basis.eq_coordPairing
declarations.doc: A pairing for which the two bases are dual is the coordinate pairing.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_coordPairing (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) (p : M ⊗[R] N →ₗ[R] R)
    (h : ∀ I J, p (b I ⊗ₜ[R] b' J) = if I = J then 1 else 0) : p = b.coordPairing b'

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing_comm
declarations.doc:
Swapping the factors swaps the bases,
`b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = b'.coordPairing b (y ⊗ₜ x)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coordPairing_comm (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    b.coordPairing b' (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) = b'.coordPairing b (y ⊗ₜ[R] x)

declarations.name: Module.Basis.isPerfPair_coordPairing
declarations.doc: The coordinate pairing of two bases with the same labels is a perfect pairing.
declarations.statement:
instance isPerfPair_coordPairing (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (b' : Module.Basis ι R N) :
    (TensorProduct.curry (b.coordPairing b')).IsPerfPair

declarations.name: Module.Basis.coordPairing_invariant
declarations.doc:
The coordinate pairing is invariant when an invariant pairing `p` makes the bases dual, since
then `p` is the coordinate pairing.

modules.title: Lie's Trace Formula
modules.doc:
This file proves the formula `det (exp A) = exp (tr A)` for matrices, also known as Lie's trace
formula.

The proof proceeds by first showing the formula for upper-triangular matrices and then
leveraging Schur triangulation to generalize to any matrix. An upper-triangular matrix `A`
is defined in `mathlib` as `Matrix.BlockTriangular A id`.

## Main results

- `Matrix.det_exp`: The determinant of the exponential of a matrix is the exponential of its trace.

sections.text: ### The determinant of the matrix exponential

declarations.statement: instance [UniformSpace 𝕂] : UniformSpace (Matrix m n 𝕂)

declarations.name: Matrix.tsum_eq_zero
declarations.doc: If every term of a series is zero, then its sum is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsum_eq_zero
    {β : Type*} [TopologicalSpace β] [AddCommMonoid β]
    {f : ℕ → β} (h : ∀ n, f n = 0) :
    (∑' n, f n) = 0

declarations.name: Matrix.matrix_tsum_apply
declarations.doc: Apply a matrix `tsum` to a given entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_tsum_apply
    {f : ℕ → Matrix m m 𝕂} (hf : Summable f) (i j : m) :
    (∑' n, f n) i j = ∑' n, (f n) i j

declarations.name: Matrix.diag_mul_of_blockTriangular_id
declarations.doc:
For upper-triangular matrices, the diagonal of a product is the product of the diagonals.
This is a specific case of a more general property for block-triangular matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma diag_mul_of_blockTriangular_id {A B : Matrix m m 𝕂}
    (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (hB : BlockTriangular B id) : (A * B).diag = A.diag * B.diag

declarations.name: Matrix.blockTriangular.pow
declarations.doc: Powers of block triangular matrices are block triangular.
declarations.statement:
lemma blockTriangular.pow {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (k : ℕ) :
    BlockTriangular (A ^ k) id

declarations.name: Matrix.diag_pow_of_blockTriangular_id
declarations.doc: For an upper-triangular matrix, the diagonal of a power is the power of the diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma diag_pow_of_blockTriangular_id {A : Matrix m m 𝕂}
    (hA : BlockTriangular A id) (k : ℕ) : (A ^ k).diag = A.diag ^ k

declarations.name: Matrix.blockTriangular_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
declarations.doc: The exponential of an upper-triangular matrix is upper-triangular.
declarations.statement:
lemma blockTriangular_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
    {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp A).BlockTriangular id

declarations.name: Matrix.diag_pow_entry_eq_pow_diag_entry
declarations.doc:
For an upper–triangular matrix `A`, the `(i,i)` entry of the power `A ^ n`
is simply the `n`-th power of the original diagonal entry.

declarations.name: Matrix.exp_series_diag_term_eq
declarations.doc:
Each term in the matrix exponential series equals the corresponding scalar term on the
diagonal
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_series_diag_term_eq {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id)
    (n : ℕ) (i : m) :
    ((n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A ^ n)) i i = (n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A i i) ^ n

declarations.name: Matrix.matrix_exp_series_diag_eq_scalar_series
declarations.doc: The diagonal of the matrix exponential series equals the scalar exponential series
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_exp_series_diag_eq_scalar_series {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id)
    (i : m) :
    (∑' n, ((n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A ^ n)) i i) = ∑' n, (n.factorial : 𝕂)⁻¹ • (A i i) ^ n

declarations.name: Matrix.diag_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
declarations.doc:
The diagonal of the exponential of an upper-triangular matrix `A` consists of the
exponentials of the diagonal entries of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem diag_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
    {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp A).diag = fun i => NormedSpace.exp (A i i)

declarations.name: Matrix.det_exp_of_blockTriangular_id
declarations.doc: Lie's trace formula for upper triangular matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma det_exp_of_blockTriangular_id {A : Matrix m m 𝕂} (hA : BlockTriangular A id) :
    (NormedSpace.exp A).det = NormedSpace.exp A.trace

declarations.name: Matrix.trace_unitary_conj
declarations.doc: The trace is invariant under unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    trace ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) = trace A

declarations.name: Matrix.det_unitary_conj
declarations.doc: The determinant is invariant under unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma det_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    det ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) = det A

declarations.name: Matrix.exp_unitary_conj
declarations.doc: The exponential of a matrix commutes with unitary conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    NormedSpace.exp ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)) =
      (U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * NormedSpace.exp A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂)

declarations.name: Matrix.det_exp_unitary_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma det_exp_unitary_conj (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) (U : unitaryGroup m 𝕂) :
    (NormedSpace.exp ((U : Matrix m m 𝕂) * A * star (U : Matrix m m 𝕂))).det =
    (NormedSpace.exp A).det

declarations.name: Matrix.det_exp
declarations.doc:
The determinant of the exponential of a matrix is the exponential of its trace.
This is also known as **Lie's trace formula**.
declarations.statement:
theorem det_exp {𝕂 m : Type*} [RCLike 𝕂] [IsAlgClosed 𝕂] [Fintype m] [LinearOrder m]
    (A : Matrix m m 𝕂) :
    (NormedSpace.exp A).det = NormedSpace.exp A.trace

declarations.name: Matrix.map_tsum
declarations.statement:
lemma map_tsum {α β m n : Type*}
    [AddCommMonoid α] [AddCommMonoid β] [TopologicalSpace α] [TopologicalSpace β]
    [T2Space β]
    (f : α →+ β) (hf : Continuous f) {s : ℕ → Matrix m n α} (hs : Summable s) :
    (∑' k, s k).map f = ∑' k, (s k).map f

declarations.name: NormedSpace.exp_map_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_map_algebraMap {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) :
    (exp A).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) = exp (A.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ))

declarations.name: Matrix.det_exp_real
declarations.doc:
Lie's trace formula over ℝ: det(exp(A)) = exp(tr(A)) for any real matrix A.
This is proved by transferring the result from ℂ using the naturality of polynomial identities.
declarations.statement:
theorem det_exp_real {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [LinearOrder n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) : (NormedSpace.exp A).det = Real.exp A.trace

modules.title: fderiv currying lemmas
modules.doc: Various lemmas related to fderiv on curried/uncurried functions.

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry (f : X → Y → Z) (xy dxy : X × Y)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (↿f) xy) :
    fderiv 𝕜 ↿f xy dxy
    =
    fderiv 𝕜 (f · xy.2) xy.1 dxy.1 + fderiv 𝕜 (f xy.1 ·) xy.2 dxy.2

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_fst (f : X × Y → Z) (x : X) (y : Y)
    (h : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f (x,y)) (dx : X) :
    fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => Function.curry f x' y) x dx = fderiv 𝕜 f (x,y) (dx, 0)

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_snd (f : X × Y → Z) (x : X) (y : Y)
    (h : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f (x,y)) (dy : Y) :
    fderiv 𝕜 (Function.curry f x) y dy = fderiv 𝕜 (f) (x,y) (0, dy)

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_clm_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_clm_comp (f : X → Y → Z) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    fderiv 𝕜 ↿f
    =
    fun xy =>
      (fderiv 𝕜 (f · xy.2) xy.1).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 X Y)
      +
      (fderiv 𝕜 (f xy.1 ·) xy.2).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 X Y)

declarations.name: fderiv_wrt_prod
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_wrt_prod {f : X × Y → Z} {xy} (hf : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f xy) :
    fderiv 𝕜 f xy
    =
    (fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => f (x',xy.2)) xy.1).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 X Y)
    +
    (fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => f (xy.1,y')) xy.2).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 X Y)

declarations.name: fderiv_wrt_prod_clm_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_wrt_prod_clm_comp (f : X × Y → Z) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 f) :
    fderiv 𝕜 f
    =
    fun xy =>
      (fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => f (x',xy.2)) xy.1).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 X Y)
      +
      (fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => f (xy.1,y')) xy.2).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 X Y)

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_clm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_clm_apply (f : X → Y →L[𝕜] Z) (y : Y) (x dx : X) (h : Differentiable 𝕜 f) :
    fderiv 𝕜 f x dx y
    =
    fderiv 𝕜 (f · y) x dx

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_comp_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_comp_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (y : Y) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => (↿f) (x', y))
    =
    fun x => (fderiv 𝕜 (↿f) ((·, y) x)).comp (fderiv 𝕜 (·, y) x)

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_comp_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_comp_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => (↿f) (x, y'))
    =
    fun y => (fderiv 𝕜 (↿f) ((x, ·) y)).comp (fderiv 𝕜 (x, ·) y)

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_comp_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_comp_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (x dx : X) (y : Y)
    (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    (fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => f x' y) x) dx
    =
    (fderiv 𝕜 (↿f) ((·, y) x)) ((fderiv 𝕜 (·, y) x) dx)

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_comp_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_comp_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (y dy : Y)
    (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    (fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => f x y') y) dy
    =
    (fderiv 𝕜 (↿f) ((x, ·) y)) ((fderiv 𝕜 (x, ·) y) dy)

declarations.name: fderiv_inr_fst_clm
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_inr_fst_clm (x : X) (y : Y) :
    (fderiv 𝕜 (x, ·) y) = ContinuousLinearMap.inr 𝕜 X Y

declarations.name: fderiv_inl_snd_clm
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_inl_snd_clm (x : X) (y : Y) :
    (fderiv 𝕜 (·, y) x) = ContinuousLinearMap.inl 𝕜 X Y

declarations.name: function_differentiableAt_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma function_differentiableAt_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (y : Y) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (fun x' => f x' y) x

declarations.name: function_differentiableAt_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma function_differentiableAt_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (y : Y) (hf : Differentiable 𝕜 (↿f)) :
    DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (fun y' => f x y') y

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (y : Y) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fderiv 𝕜 fun x' => (↿f) (x', y))

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fderiv 𝕜 fun y' => (↿f) (x, y'))

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst_comp_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst_comp_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fun y' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => (↿f) (x', y')) x)

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst_comp_snd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_fst_comp_snd_apply (f : X → Y → Z) (x δx : X)
    (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fun y' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => (↿f) (x', y')) x δx)

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd_comp_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd_comp_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (y : Y) (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fun x' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => (↿f) (x', y')) y)

declarations.name: fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd_comp_fst_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_uncurry_differentiable_snd_comp_fst_apply (f : X → Y → Z) (y δy : Y)
    (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    Differentiable 𝕜 (fun x' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => (↿f) (x', y')) y δy)

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_differentiableAt_fst_comp_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_differentiableAt_fst_comp_snd (f : X → Y → Z) (x dx : X) (y : Y)
    (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (fun y' => (fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => f x' y') x) dx) y

declarations.name: fderiv_curry_differentiableAt_snd_comp_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_curry_differentiableAt_snd_comp_fst (f : X → Y → Z) (x : X) (y dy : Y)
    (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    DifferentiableAt 𝕜 (fun x' => (fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => f x' y') y) dy) x

declarations.name: fderiv_swap
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_swap [IsRCLikeNormedField 𝕜] (f : X → Y → Z) (x dx : X) (y dy : Y)
    (hf : ContDiff 𝕜 2 ↿f) :
    fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => f x' y') y dy) x dx
    =
    fderiv 𝕜 (fun y' => fderiv 𝕜 (fun x' => f x' y') x dx) y dy

modules.title: Fin lemmas
modules.doc:
The purpose of this file is to define some results Fin currently
in Mathlib.

At some point these should either be up-streamed to Mathlib or replaced with definitions already
in Mathlib.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI
declarations.doc:
Given a `i` and `x` in `Fin n.succ.succ` returns an element of `Fin n.succ`
subtracting 1 if `i.val ≤ x.val` else casting x.
declarations.statement: def predAboveI (i x : Fin n.succ.succ) : Fin n.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI_self
declarations.statement: lemma predAboveI_self (i : Fin n.succ.succ) : predAboveI i i = ⟨i.val - 1, by omega⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI_succAbove
declarations.statement:
lemma predAboveI_succAbove (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (x : Fin n.succ) :
    predAboveI i (Fin.succAbove i x) = x

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.succsAbove_predAboveI
declarations.statement:
lemma succsAbove_predAboveI {i x : Fin n.succ.succ} (h : i ≠ x) :
    Fin.succAbove i (predAboveI i x) = x

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma predAboveI_eq_iff {i x : Fin n.succ.succ} (h : i ≠ x) (y : Fin n.succ) :
    y = predAboveI i x ↔ i.succAbove y = x

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma predAboveI_lt {i x : Fin n.succ.succ} (h : x.val < i.val) :
    predAboveI i x = ⟨x.val, by omega⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.predAboveI_ge
declarations.statement:
lemma predAboveI_ge {i x : Fin n.succ.succ} (h : i.val < x.val) :
    predAboveI i x = ⟨x.val - 1, by omega⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.succAbove_succAbove_predAboveI
declarations.statement:
lemma succAbove_succAbove_predAboveI (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) (x : Fin n) :
    i.succAbove (j.succAbove x) =
    (i.succAbove j).succAbove ((predAboveI (i.succAbove j) i).succAbove x)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `Fin n.succ` and `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n` extracting the
`i`th component.
declarations.statement: def finExtractOne {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 1)) : Fin (n + 1) ≃ Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne_apply_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOne_apply_eq {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ) :
    finExtractOne i i = Sum.inl 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne_symm_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOne_symm_inr {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ) :
    (finExtractOne i).symm ∘ Sum.inr = i.succAbove

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne_symm_inr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOne_symm_inr_apply {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ) (x : Fin n) :
    (finExtractOne i).symm (Sum.inr x) = i.succAbove x

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne_symm_inl_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOne_symm_inl_apply {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ) :
    (finExtractOne i).symm (Sum.inl 0) = i

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOne_apply_neq
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOne_apply_neq {n : ℕ} (i j : Fin (n + 1 + 1)) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    finExtractOne i j = Sum.inr (predAboveI i j)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnPermHom
declarations.doc:
Given an equivalence `Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin n.succ.succ`, and an `i : Fin n.succ.succ`,
the map `Fin n.succ → Fin n.succ` obtained by dropping `i` and it's image.
declarations.statement:
def finExtractOnPermHom {m : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (σ : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin m.succ.succ) :
    Fin n.succ → Fin m.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnPermHom_inv
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOnPermHom_inv {m : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ)
    (σ : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin m.succ.succ) :
    (finExtractOnPermHom (σ i) σ.symm) ∘ (finExtractOnPermHom i σ) = id

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnePerm
declarations.doc:
Given an equivalence `Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin n.succ.succ`, and an `i : Fin n.succ.succ`,
the equivalence `Fin n.succ ≃ Fin n.succ` obtained by dropping `i` and it's image.
declarations.statement:
def finExtractOnePerm {m : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (σ : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin m.succ.succ) :
    Fin n.succ ≃ Fin m.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnePerm_equiv
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOnePerm_equiv {n m : ℕ} (e : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin m.succ.succ)
    (i : Fin n.succ.succ) :
    e ∘ i.succAbove = (e i).succAbove ∘ finExtractOnePerm i e

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnePerm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOnePerm_apply (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (σ : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin n.succ.succ)
    (x : Fin n.succ) : finExtractOnePerm i σ x = predAboveI (σ i)
    (σ ((finExtractOne i).symm (Sum.inr x)))

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractOnePerm_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractOnePerm_symm_apply (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (σ : Fin n.succ.succ ≃ Fin n.succ.succ)
    (x : Fin n.succ) : (finExtractOnePerm i σ).symm x = predAboveI (σ.symm (σ i))
    (σ.symm ((finExtractOne (σ i)).symm (Sum.inr x)))

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo
declarations.doc:
The equivalence of types `Fin n.succ.succ ≃ (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin n` extracting
the `i` and `(i.succAbove j)`.
declarations.statement:
def finExtractTwo {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    Fin n.succ.succ ≃ (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1) ⊕ Fin n

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_apply_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_apply_fst {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    finExtractTwo i j i = Sum.inl (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_symm_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_symm_inr {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    (finExtractTwo i j).symm ∘ Sum.inr = i.succAbove ∘ j.succAbove

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_symm_inr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_symm_inr_apply {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) (x : Fin n) :
    (finExtractTwo i j).symm (Sum.inr x) = i.succAbove (j.succAbove x)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_symm_inl_inr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_symm_inl_inr_apply {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    (finExtractTwo i j).symm (Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0)) = i.succAbove j

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_symm_inl_inl_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_symm_inl_inl_apply {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    (finExtractTwo i j).symm (Sum.inl (Sum.inl 0)) = i

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finExtractTwo_apply_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma finExtractTwo_apply_snd {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n.succ.succ) (j : Fin n.succ) :
    finExtractTwo i j (i.succAbove j) = Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finMapToEquiv
declarations.doc: Takes two maps `Fin n → Fin n` and returns the equivalence they form.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.finMapToEquiv_apply
Physlib.Fin.finMapToEquiv_symm_apply
Physlib.Fin.finMapToEquiv_symm_eq
Physlib.Fin.equivCons
declarations.doc:
Given an equivalence between `Fin n` and `Fin m`, the induced equivalence between
`Fin n.succ` and `Fin m.succ` derived by `Fin.cons`.
declarations.statement: def equivCons {n m : ℕ} (e : Fin n ≃ Fin m) : Fin n.succ ≃ Fin m.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.equivCons_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma equivCons_zero {n m : ℕ} (e : Fin n ≃ Fin m) :
    equivCons e 0 = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.equivCons_trans
declarations.statement:
lemma equivCons_trans {n m k : ℕ} (e : Fin n ≃ Fin m) (f : Fin m ≃ Fin k) :
    Fin.equivCons (e.trans f) = (Fin.equivCons e).trans (Fin.equivCons f)

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.equivCons_castOrderIso
declarations.statement:
lemma equivCons_castOrderIso {n m : ℕ} (h : n = m) :

modules.title: Fin involutions
modules.doc:
Some properties of involutions of `Fin n`.

These involutions are used in e.g. proving results about Wick contractions.

sections.text:
## Equivalences of involutions with no fixed points.

The main aim of these equivalences is to define `involutionNoFixedZeroEquivProd`.
## Cardinality

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionCons
declarations.doc:
There is an equivalence between involutions of `Fin n.succ` and involutions of
`Fin n` and an optional valid choice of an element in `Fin n` (which is where `0`
  in `Fin n.succ` will be sent).

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionCons_ext
Physlib.Fin.involutionAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
Given an involution of `Fin n`, the optional choice of an element in `Fin n` which
maps to itself is equivalent to the optional choice of an element in
`Fin (Finset.univ.filter fun i => f.1 i = i).card`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionAddEquiv_none_image_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma involutionAddEquiv_none_image_zero {n : ℕ} :
    {f : {f : Fin n.succ → Fin n.succ // Function.Involutive f}}
    → involutionAddEquiv (involutionCons n f).1 (involutionCons n f).2 = none
    → f.1 ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ n⟩ = ⟨0, Nat.zero_lt_succ n⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionAddEquiv_cast
declarations.statement:
lemma involutionAddEquiv_cast {n : ℕ} {f1 f2 : {f : Fin n → Fin n // Function.Involutive f}}
    (hf : f1 = f2) :
    involutionAddEquiv f1 = (Equiv.subtypeEquivRight (by rw [hf]; simp)).trans
      ((involutionAddEquiv f2).trans (Equiv.optionCongr (finCongr (by rw [hf]))))

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionAddEquiv_cast'
declarations.statement:
lemma involutionAddEquiv_cast' {m : ℕ} {f1 f2 : {f : Fin m → Fin m // Function.Involutive f}}
    {N : ℕ} (hf : f1 = f2) (n : Option (Fin N))
    (hn1 : N = (Finset.filter (fun i => f1.1 i = i) Finset.univ).card)
    (hn2 : N = (Finset.filter (fun i => f2.1 i = i) Finset.univ).card) :
    HEq ((involutionAddEquiv f1).symm (Option.map (finCongr hn1) n))
    ((involutionAddEquiv f2).symm (Option.map (finCongr hn2) n))

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionAddEquiv_none_succ
Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedEquivSum
declarations.doc:
Fixed point free involutions of `Fin n.succ` can be separated based on where they sent
`0`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroSetEquivEquiv
declarations.doc:
The condition on fixed point free involutions of `Fin n.succ` for a fixed value of `f 0`,
can be modified by conjugation with an equivalence.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroSetEquivSetEquiv
declarations.doc:
The condition on fixed point free involutions of `Fin n.succ` for a fixed value of `f 0`
given an equivalence `e`,
can be modified so that only the condition on `f 0` is up-to the equivalence `e`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroSetEquivEquiv'
declarations.doc:
Fixed point free involutions of `Fin n.succ` fixing `(e.symm ∘ f ∘ e) = k.succ` for a given `e`
are equivalent to fixing `f (e 0) = e k.succ`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroSetEquivSetOne
declarations.doc:
Fixed point involutions of `Fin n.succ.succ` with `f 0 = k.succ` are equivalent
to fixed point involutions with `f 0 = 1`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedSetOne
declarations.doc:
Fixed point involutions of `Fin n.succ.succ` fixing `f 0 = 1` are equivalent to
fixed point involutions of `Fin n`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroSetEquiv
declarations.doc:
Fixed point involutions of `Fin n.succ.succ` for fixed `f 0 = k.succ` are
equivalent to fixed point involutions of `Fin n`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedEquivSumSame
declarations.doc:
The type of fixed point free involutions of `Fin n.succ.succ` is equivalent to the sum
of `Fin n.succ` copies of fixed point involutions of `Fin n`.

declarations.name: Physlib.Fin.involutionNoFixedZeroEquivProd
declarations.doc:
Ever fixed-point free involutions of `Fin n.succ.succ` can be decomposed into a
element of `Fin n.succ` (where `0` is sent) and a fixed-point free involution of
`Fin n`.
The type of fixed-point free involutions of `Fin n` is finite.

modules.title: Basic integration results
modules.doc:
Basic results related to integration not in Mathlib.

## i. Overview

Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul` converts an integral against a
measure `μ.withDensity f` into an integral against `μ`, but it takes the density as an
`NNReal`-valued function.

This file contains the version of that lemma for densities given as real-valued functions.

## ii. Key results

- `Integration.integral_withDensity_ofReal_eq_integral_smul` : for measurable `f ≥ 0`,
  `∫ x, g x ∂(μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) = ∫ x, f x • g x ∂μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integrals against a real-valued density

## iv. References

sections.text: ## A. Integrals against a real-valued density

declarations.name: Integration.integral_withDensity_ofReal_eq_integral_smul
declarations.doc:
Integrating `g` against the measure with real-valued density `f` (taken through
`ENNReal.ofReal`) is integrating `f x • g x` against the original measure, for measurable
`f` that is everywhere nonnegative. This is the `ℝ`-valued form of
`integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul`, which takes an `NNReal`-valued density.
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_withDensity_ofReal_eq_integral_smul {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α]
    {μ : Measure α} {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (hf0 : ∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) (g : α → E) :
    ∫ x, g x ∂(μ.withDensity fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (f x)) = ∫ x, f x • g x ∂μ

modules.title: LinearPMap
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we collect some basic results about `LinearPMap`s.

Most important is the definition of restricted composition.
The composition of two partial linear maps `g : F →ₗ.[R] G` and `f : E →ₗ.[R] F` is defined
only if the range of `f` is contained in the domain of `g` (c.f. `LinearPMap.comp`).
`g.compRestricted f` (`g ∘ᵣ f`) is defined to be the composition of `g` with the restriction of `f`
to exactly those `x : f.domain` for which `f x ∈ g.domain`. This allows one to work with the
composition of partial linear maps while having the domain implicitly accounted for.

## ii. Key results

- `LinearPMap.sum` : The finite sum of partial linear maps.
- `LinearPMap.compRestricted` (`∘ᵣ`) : For two partial linear maps
    `g : F →ₗ[R] G` and `f : E →ₗ[R] F`, the composition of `g` with `f`
    with natural domain `{x : f.domain | f x ∈ g.domain}`.
- `LinearPMap.instMonoid` : Partial linear maps `E →ₗ.[R] E` with `compRestricted`
    for multiplication and the identity map for `1` comprise a monoid.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Inequalities
- B. Zero smul
- C. Finite sums
- D. Restricted composition
- E. Monoid
- F. Inverses

## iv. References

* None.

## E. Monoid

A finite sum of partial linear maps.
