declarations.name: LinearPMap.sum_domain_le
declarations.statement: lemma sum_domain_le (a : α) : (sum f).domain ≤ (f a).domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.sum_apply
declarations.statement: lemma sum_apply (ψ : (sum f).domain) : sum f ψ = ∑ a, f a ⟨ψ, sum_domain_le f a ψ.2⟩

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted
declarations.doc:
`g ∘ᵣ f` is the composition of `g` with `f` restricted to a domain consisting of exactly those
`x : f.domain` for which `f x ∈ g.domain`.
declarations.statement: def compRestricted : E →ₗ.[R] G

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_domain_le
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_domain_le : (g ∘ᵣ f).domain ≤ f.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_domain
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_domain : (g ∘ᵣ f).domain = (g.domain.comap f.toFun).map f.domain.subtype

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_compRestricted_domain_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_compRestricted_domain_iff {x : E} :
    x ∈ (v ∘ᵣ u).domain ↔ ∃ h : x ∈ u.domain, u ⟨x, h⟩ ∈ v.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_compRestricted_domain_iff'
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_compRestricted_domain_iff' {x : E} :
    x ∈ (v ∘ᵣ u).domain ↔ ∃ y : u.domain, x = y ∧ ∃ y' : v.domain, u y = y'

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_domain_of_mem_compRestricted_domain
declarations.statement: lemma mem_domain_of_mem_compRestricted_domain (x : (v ∘ᵣ u).domain) : u ⟨x, x.2.2⟩ ∈ v.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_apply (x : (v ∘ᵣ u).domain) :
    (v ∘ᵣ u) x = v ⟨u ⟨x, x.2.2⟩, mem_domain_of_mem_compRestricted_domain x⟩

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_zero
declarations.doc: The zero map is right-absorbing.
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_zero : g ∘ᵣ (0 : E →ₗ.[R] F) = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_assoc
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_assoc {H : Type*} [AddCommGroup H] [Module R H]
    (f₁ : G →ₗ.[R] H) (f₂ : F →ₗ.[R] G) (f₃ : E →ₗ.[R] F) :
    (f₁ ∘ᵣ f₂) ∘ᵣ f₃ = f₁ ∘ᵣ f₂ ∘ᵣ f₃

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_eq_comp
declarations.doc: `compRestricted` is the same as `comp` when the range of `u` is contained in `v.domain`.
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_eq_comp (h : ∀ x : u.domain, u x ∈ v.domain) :
    v ∘ᵣ u = v.comp u h

declarations.name: LinearPMap.comp_le_compRestricted
declarations.doc: `compRestricted` is maximal amongst compositions of `v` with domain restrictions of `u`.
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_le_compRestricted
    {S : Submodule R E} (h : ∀ x : (u.domRestrict S).domain, u ⟨x, x.2.2⟩ ∈ v.domain) :
    v.comp (u.domRestrict S) h ≤ v ∘ᵣ u

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_mono_left
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_mono_left {g g' : F →ₗ.[R] G} (h : g ≤ g') (f : E →ₗ.[R] F) :
    g ∘ᵣ f ≤ g' ∘ᵣ f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_mono_right
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_mono_right (g : F →ₗ.[R] G) {f f' : E →ₗ.[R] F} (h : f ≤ f') :
    g ∘ᵣ f ≤ g ∘ᵣ f'

declarations.name: LinearPMap.neg_compRestricted
declarations.statement: lemma neg_compRestricted : (-g) ∘ᵣ f = -g ∘ᵣ f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_neg
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_neg : g ∘ᵣ (-f) = -g ∘ᵣ f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.add_compRestricted
declarations.statement: lemma add_compRestricted : (g₁ + g₂) ∘ᵣ f = g₁ ∘ᵣ f + g₂ ∘ᵣ f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.sub_compRestricted
declarations.statement: lemma sub_compRestricted : (g₁ - g₂) ∘ᵣ f = g₁ ∘ᵣ f - g₂ ∘ᵣ f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_add_ge
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_add_ge : g ∘ᵣ f₁ + g ∘ᵣ f₂ ≤ g ∘ᵣ (f₁ + f₂)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_sub_ge
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_sub_ge : g ∘ᵣ f₁ - g ∘ᵣ f₂ ≤ g ∘ᵣ (f₁ - f₂)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma compRestricted_smul {S : Type*} [DivisionRing S]
    [Module S E] [Module S F] [Module S G] [SMulCommClass S S F] [SMulCommClass S S G]
    {c : S} (hc : c ≠ 0) (g : F →ₗ.[S] G) (f : E →ₗ.[S] F) :
    g ∘ᵣ (c • f) = c • (g ∘ᵣ f)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.smul_compRestricted
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_compRestricted {M : Type*} [Monoid M] [DistribMulAction M G] [SMulCommClass R M G]
    (c : M) (g : F →ₗ.[R] G) (f : E →ₗ.[R] F) :
    (c • g) ∘ᵣ f = c • (g ∘ᵣ f)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.instMonoid
declarations.statement: instance instMonoid : Monoid (E →ₗ.[R] E)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mul_def
declarations.statement: lemma mul_def (f₁ f₂ : E →ₗ.[R] E) : f₁ * f₂ = f₁ ∘ᵣ f₂

declarations.name: LinearPMap.one_domain
declarations.statement: lemma one_domain : (1 : E →ₗ.[R] E).domain = ⊤

declarations.name: LinearPMap.one_toFun
declarations.statement: lemma one_toFun : (1 : E →ₗ.[R] E).toFun = topEquiv.toLinearMap

declarations.name: LinearPMap.one_coe
declarations.statement: lemma one_coe : (1 : E →ₗ.[R] E).toFun' = ⇑topEquiv.toLinearMap

declarations.name: LinearPMap.toFun_ker_eq_bot_iff
declarations.doc: The kernel of `f.toFun` is trivial exactly when the kernel of `f` is.
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_ker_eq_bot_iff {f : E →ₗ.[R] F} : f.toFun.ker = ⊥ ↔ f.ker = ⊥

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inverse_ker
declarations.statement: lemma inverse_ker : f.inverse.toFun.ker = ⊥

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inverse_inverse
declarations.statement: lemma inverse_inverse : f.inverse.inverse = f

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inverse_compRestricted_eq
declarations.statement: lemma inverse_compRestricted_eq : f.inverse ∘ᵣ f = domRestrict 1 f.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compRestricted_inverse_eq
declarations.statement: lemma compRestricted_inverse_eq : f ∘ᵣ f.inverse = domRestrict 1 f.inverse.domain

declarations.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_eraseIdx
declarations.statement:
lemma takeWhile_eraseIdx {I : Type} (P : I → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    (l : List I) → (i : ℕ) → (hi : ∀ (i j : Fin l.length), i < j → P (l.get j) → P (l.get i)) →
    List.takeWhile P (List.eraseIdx l i) = (List.takeWhile P l).eraseIdx i

declarations.name: Physlib.List.dropWile_eraseIdx
declarations.statement:
lemma dropWile_eraseIdx {I : Type} (P : I → Prop) [DecidablePred P] :
    (l : List I) → (i : ℕ) → (hi : ∀ (i j : Fin l.length), i < j → P (l.get j) → P (l.get i)) →
    List.dropWhile P (List.eraseIdx l i) =
      if (List.takeWhile P l).length ≤ i then
        (List.dropWhile P l).eraseIdx (i - (List.takeWhile P l).length)
      else (List.dropWhile P l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_length
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_length {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (l : List I) :
    (List.insertionSort le1 l).length = l.length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos
declarations.doc: The position `r0` ends up in `r` on adding it via `List.orderedInsert _ r0 r`.
declarations.statement:
def orderedInsertPos {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    Fin (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_lt_length
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_lt_length {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) : orderedInsertPos le1 r r0 < (r0 :: r).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_get_orderedInsertPos
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_get_orderedInsertPos {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)[(orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).val] = r0

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertPos
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertPos {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx ↑(orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) = r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_cons {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 r1 : I) :
    (orderedInsertPos le1 (r1 ::r) r0).val =
    if le1 r0 r1 then ⟨0, by simp⟩ else (Fin.succ (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_sigma
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_sigma {I : Type} {f : I → Type}
    (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (l : List (Σ i, f i))
    (k : I) (a : f k) :
    (orderedInsertPos (fun (i j : Σ i, f i) => le1 i.1 j.1) l ⟨k, a⟩).1 =
    (orderedInsertPos le1 (List.map (fun (i : Σ i, f i) => i.1) l) k).1

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_get_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_get_lt {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) (i : ℕ)
    (hi : i < orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)[i] = r.get ⟨i, by
      simp only [orderedInsertPos] at hi
      have h1 : (List.takeWhile (fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b) r).length ≤ r.length :=
        List.Sublist.length_le (List.takeWhile_sublist fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b)
      omega⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_take_orderedInsert
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_take_orderedInsert {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    (List.take (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)) =
    List.takeWhile (fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b) r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_take_eq_orderedInsert
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_take_eq_orderedInsert {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    List.take (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) r =
    List.take (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_drop_eq_orderedInsert
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_drop_eq_orderedInsert {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    List.drop (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) r =
    List.drop (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).succ (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_take
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_take {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    List.take (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) r = List.takeWhile (fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b) r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_drop {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    List.drop (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0) r = List.dropWhile (fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b) r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertPos_succ_take_orderedInsert
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertPos_succ_take_orderedInsert {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    (List.take (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).succ (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r)) =
    List.takeWhile (fun b => decide ¬le1 r0 b) r ++ [r0]

declarations.name: Physlib.List.lt_orderedInsertPos_rel
declarations.statement:
lemma lt_orderedInsertPos_rel {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r0 : I) (r : List I) (n : Fin r.length)
    (hn : n.val < (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).val) : ¬ le1 r0 (r.get n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.lt_orderedInsertPos_rel_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma lt_orderedInsertPos_rel_fin {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r0 : I) (r : List I) (n : Fin (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).length)
    (hn : n < (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0)) : ¬ le1 r0 ((List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).get n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.gt_orderedInsertPos_rel
declarations.statement:
lemma gt_orderedInsertPos_rel {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    [Std.Total le1] [IsTrans I le1] (r0 : I) (r : List I) (hs : List.Pairwise le1 r)
    (n : Fin r.length)
    (hn : ¬ n.val < (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).val) : le1 r0 (r.get n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_lt_orderedInsertPos
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_lt_orderedInsertPos {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) (i : ℕ)
    (hi : i < orderedInsertPos le1 r r0)
    (hr : ∀ (i j : Fin r.length), i < j → ¬le1 r0 (r.get j) → ¬le1 r0 (r.get i)) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx i = List.orderedInsert le1 r0 (r.eraseIdx i)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertPos_le
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertPos_le {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) (i : ℕ)
    (hi : orderedInsertPos le1 r r0 ≤ i)
    (hr : ∀ (i j : Fin r.length), i < j → ¬le1 r0 (r.get j) → ¬le1 r0 (r.get i)) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx (Nat.succ i) =
    List.orderedInsert le1 r0 (r.eraseIdx i)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `Fin (r0 :: r).length` and `Fin (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).length`
according to where the elements map, i.e. `0` is taken to `orderedInsertPos le1 r r0`.
declarations.statement:
def orderedInsertEquiv {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    Fin (r.length + 1) ≃ Fin (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_zero {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) : orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 0 = orderedInsertPos le1 r r0

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_succ {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) (n : ℕ) (hn : Nat.succ n < (r0 :: r).length) :
    orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 ⟨Nat.succ n, hn⟩ =
    Fin.cast (List.orderedInsert_length le1 r r0).symm
    ((Fin.succAbove ⟨(orderedInsertPos le1 r r0), orderedInsertPos_lt_length le1 r r0⟩)
    ⟨n, Nat.succ_lt_succ_iff.mp hn⟩)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_fin_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_fin_succ {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) (n : Fin r.length) :
    orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 n.succ = Fin.cast (List.orderedInsert_length le1 r r0).symm
    ((Fin.succAbove ⟨(orderedInsertPos le1 r r0), orderedInsertPos_lt_length le1 r r0⟩)
      ⟨n, n.isLt⟩)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_monotone_fin_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_monotone_fin_succ {I : Type}
    (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) (n m : Fin r.length)
    (hx : orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 n.succ < orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 m.succ) :
    n < m

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_congr {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] (a : α)
    (l l' : List α) (h : l = l') :
    orderedInsertEquiv r l a = (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp [h])).toEquiv.trans
    ((orderedInsertEquiv r l' a).trans (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp [h])).toEquiv)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.get_eq_orderedInsertEquiv
declarations.statement:
lemma get_eq_orderedInsertEquiv {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) :
    (r0 :: r).get = (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).get ∘ (orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_get
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_get {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I)
    (r0 : I) :
    (r0 :: r).get ∘ (orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0).symm = (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).get

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_zero
    {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx (orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 ⟨0, by simp⟩) = r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_succ
    {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I) (r0 : I) (n : ℕ)
    (hn : Nat.succ n < (r0 :: r).length)
    (hr : ∀ (i j : Fin r.length), i < j → ¬le1 r0 (r.get j) → ¬le1 r0 (r.get i)) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx (orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 ⟨Nat.succ n, hn⟩) =
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 (r.eraseIdx n))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_fin_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eraseIdx_orderedInsertEquiv_fin_succ
    {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (r : List I) (r0 : I) (n : Fin r.length)
    (hr : ∀ (i j : Fin r.length), i < j → ¬le1 r0 (r.get j) → ¬le1 r0 (r.get i)) :
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r).eraseIdx (orderedInsertEquiv le1 r r0 n.succ) =
    (List.orderedInsert le1 r0 (r.eraseIdx n))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsertEquiv_sigma
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsertEquiv_sigma {I : Type} {f : I → Type}
    (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1] (l : List (Σ i, f i))
    (i : I) (a : f i) :
    (orderedInsertEquiv (fun i j => le1 i.fst j.fst) l ⟨i, a⟩) =
    (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp)).toEquiv.trans
    ((orderedInsertEquiv le1 (List.map (fun i => i.1) l) i).trans
    (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp [List.orderedInsert_length])).toEquiv)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_eq_insertIdx_orderedInsertPos
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_eq_insertIdx_orderedInsertPos {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    (r : List I) (r0 : I) :
    List.orderedInsert le1 r0 r = List.insertIdx r (orderedInsertPos le1 r r0).1 r0

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `Fin l.length ≃ Fin (List.insertionSort r l).length` induced by the
sorting algorithm.
declarations.statement:
def insertionSortEquiv {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] : (l : List α) →
    Fin l.length ≃ Fin (List.insertionSort r l).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_get
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_get {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] : (l : List α) →
    l.get ∘ (insertionSortEquiv r l).symm = (List.insertionSort r l).get

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_congr {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] (l l' : List α)
    (h : l = l') : insertionSortEquiv r l = (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp [h])).toEquiv.trans
      ((insertionSortEquiv r l').trans (Fin.castOrderIso (by simp [h])).toEquiv)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_congr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_congr_apply {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] (l l' : List α)
    (h : l = l') (i : Fin l.length) :
    insertionSortEquiv r l i =
    Fin.cast (by simp [h])
    ((insertionSortEquiv r l') (Fin.cast (by simp [h]) i))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_get_comp_insertionSortEquiv
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_get_comp_insertionSortEquiv {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r]
    (l : List α) : (List.insertionSort r l).get ∘ (insertionSortEquiv r l) = l.get

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_eq_ofFn
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_eq_ofFn {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] (l : List α) :
    List.insertionSort r l = List.ofFn (l.get ∘ (insertionSortEquiv r l).symm)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_order
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_order {α : Type} {r : α → α → Prop} [DecidableRel r] :
    (l : List α) → (i : Fin l.length) → (j : Fin l.length) → (hij : i < j)
    → (hij' : insertionSortEquiv r l j < insertionSortEquiv r l i) →
    ¬ r l[i] l[j]

declarations.name: Physlib.List.optionErase
declarations.doc:
Optional erase of an element in a list. For `none` returns the list, for `some i` returns
the list with the `i`'th element erased.
declarations.statement: def optionErase {I : Type} (l : List I) (i : Option (Fin l.length)) : List I

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_length'
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_length' {I : Type} (l : List I) (i : Fin l.length) :
    (List.eraseIdx l i).length = l.length - 1

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_length
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_length {I : Type} (l : List I) (i : Fin l.length) :
    (List.eraseIdx l i).length + 1 = l.length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_length_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_length_succ {I : Type} (l : List I) (i : Fin l.length) :
    (List.eraseIdx l i).length.succ = l.length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_cons_length
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_cons_length {I : Type} (a : I) (l : List I) (i : Fin (a :: l).length) :
    (List.eraseIdx (a :: l) i).length= l.length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_get
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_get {I : Type} (l : List I) (i : Fin l.length) :
    (List.eraseIdx l i).get = l.get ∘ (Fin.cast (eraseIdx_length l i)) ∘
    (Fin.cast (eraseIdx_length l i).symm i).succAbove

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_insertionSort
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_insertionSort {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    [Std.Total le1] [IsTrans I le1] :
    (n : ℕ) → (r : List I) → (hn : n < r.length) →
    (List.insertionSort le1 r).eraseIdx ↑((insertionSortEquiv le1 r) ⟨n, hn⟩)
    = List.insertionSort le1 (r.eraseIdx n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_insertionSort_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_insertionSort_fin {I : Type} (le1 : I → I → Prop) [DecidableRel le1]
    [Std.Total le1] [IsTrans I le1] (r : List I) (n : Fin r.length) :
    (List.insertionSort le1 r).eraseIdx ↑((Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv le1 r) n)
    = List.insertionSort le1 (r.eraseIdx n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMinPos
declarations.doc:
Given a list `i :: l` the left-most minimal position `a` of `i :: l` wrt `r`.
That is the first position
of `l` such that for every element `(i :: l)[b]` before that position
`r ((i :: l)[b]) ((i :: l)[a])` is not true. The use of `i :: l` here
rather then just `l` is to ensure that such a position exists. .
declarations.statement:
def insertionSortMinPos {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] (i : α) (l : List α) :
    Fin (i :: l).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMin
declarations.doc: The element of `i :: l` at `insertionSortMinPos`.
declarations.statement:
def insertionSortMin {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] (i : α) (l : List α) :
    α

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMin_eq_insertionSort_head
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortMin_eq_insertionSort_head {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (i : α) (l : List α) :
    insertionSortMin r i l = (List.insertionSort r (i :: l)).head (by
    refine List.ne_nil_of_length_pos ?_
    rw [insertionSort_length]
    exact Nat.zero_lt_succ l.length)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortDropMinPos
declarations.doc:
The list remaining after dropping the element at the position determined by
`insertionSortMinPos`.
declarations.statement:
def insertionSortDropMinPos {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] (i : α) (l : List α) :
    List α

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_eq_insertionSortMin_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_eq_insertionSortMin_cons {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (i : α) (l : List α) :
    List.insertionSort r (i :: l) =
    (insertionSortMin r i l) :: List.insertionSort r (insertionSortDropMinPos r i l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.optionEraseZ
declarations.doc:
Optional erase of an element in a list, with addition for `none`. For `none` adds `a` to the
front of the list, for `some i` removes the `i`th element of the list (does not add `a`).
E.g. `optionEraseZ [0, 1, 2] 4 none = [4, 0, 1, 2]` and
`optionEraseZ [0, 1, 2] 4 (some 1) = [0, 2]`.
declarations.statement: def optionEraseZ {I : Type} (l : List I) (a : I) (i : Option (Fin l.length)) : List I

declarations.name: Physlib.List.optionEraseZ_some_length
declarations.statement:
lemma optionEraseZ_some_length {I : Type} (l : List I) (a : I) (i : (Fin l.length)) :
    (optionEraseZ l a (some i)).length = l.length - 1

declarations.name: Physlib.List.optionEraseZ_ext
declarations.statement:
lemma optionEraseZ_ext {I : Type} {l l' : List I} {a a' : I} {i : Option (Fin l.length)}
    {i' : Option (Fin l'.length)} (hl : l = l') (ha : a = a')
    (hi : Option.map (Fin.cast (by rw [hl])) i = i') :
    optionEraseZ l a i = optionEraseZ l' a' i'

declarations.name: Physlib.List.mem_take_finrange
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_take_finrange : (n m : ℕ) → (a : Fin n) → a ∈ List.take m (List.finRange n) ↔ a.val < m
  | 0, m, a => Fin.elim0 a
  | n+1, 0, a => by
    simp
  | n +1, m + 1, ⟨0, h⟩ => by
    simp [List.finRange_succ]
  | n +1, m + 1, ⟨i + 1, h⟩ => by
    simp only [List.finRange_succ, List.take_succ_cons, List.mem_cons, Fin.ext_iff, Fin.val_zero,
      Nat.add_eq_zero_iff, one_ne_zero, and_false, false_or, add_lt_add_iff_right]
    rw [← List.map_take, @List.mem_map]
    apply Iff.intro
    · intro h
      obtain ⟨a, ha⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_map
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_map {I J : Type} (f : I → J) : (i : ℕ) → (r : List I) → (r0 : I) →
    (List.insertIdx r i r0).map f = List.insertIdx (r.map f) i (f r0)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.eraseIdx_sorted
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdx_sorted {I : Type} (le : I → I → Prop) :
    (r : List I) → (n : ℕ) →
    List.Pairwise le r → List.Pairwise le (r.eraseIdx n)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.mem_eraseIdx_nodup
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_eraseIdx_nodup {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (l : List I) → (n : ℕ) → (hn : n < l.length) → (h : List.Nodup l) →
    i ∈ l.eraseIdx n ↔ i ∈ l ∧ i ≠ l[n]
  | [], _, _, _ => by simp
  | a1 :: as, 0, _, h => by
    simp only [List.eraseIdx_zero, List.tail_cons, List.mem_cons, List.getElem_cons_zero, ne_eq]
    by_cases hi : i = a1
    · subst hi
      simp only [List.nodup_cons] at h
      simp [h]
    · simp [hi]
  | a1 :: as, n+1, hn, h => by
    simp only [List.eraseIdx_cons_succ, List.mem_cons, List.getElem_cons_succ, ne_eq]
    simp only [List.nodup_cons] at h
    rw [mem_eraseIdx_nodup i as n (Nat.succ_lt_succ_iff.mp hn) h.2]
    simp_all only [ne_eq]
    obtain ⟨left, right⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_eq_take_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_eq_take_drop {I : Type} (i : I) : (r : List I) → (n : Fin r.length.succ) →
    List.insertIdx r n i = List.take n r ++ i :: r.drop n

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_length_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_length_fin {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (r : List I) → (n : Fin r.length.succ) →
    (List.insertIdx r n i).length = r.length.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_getElem_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_getElem_fin {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (r : List I) → (k : Fin r.length.succ) → (m : Fin r.length) →
    (List.insertIdx r k i)[(k.succAbove m).val] = r[m.val]

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_eraseIdx_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_eraseIdx_fin {I : Type} :
    (r : List I) → (k : Fin r.length) →
    (List.eraseIdx r k).insertIdx k r[k] = r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertIdx_length_fst_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertIdx_length_fst_append {I : Type} (φ : I) : (φs φs' : List I) →
    List.insertIdx (φs ++ φs') φs.length φ = (φs ++ φ :: φs')

declarations.name: Physlib.List.get_eq_insertIdx_succAbove
declarations.statement:
lemma get_eq_insertIdx_succAbove {I : Type} (i : I) (r : List I) (k : Fin r.length.succ) :
    r.get = (List.insertIdx r k i).get ∘
    (finCongr (insertIdx_length_fin i r k).symm) ∘ k.succAbove

declarations.name: Physlib.List.take_insert_same
declarations.statement:
lemma take_insert_same {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (n : ℕ) → (r : List I) →
    List.take n (List.insertIdx r n i) = List.take n r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.take_eraseIdx_same
declarations.statement:
lemma take_eraseIdx_same {I : Type} :
    (n : ℕ) → (r : List I) →
    List.take n (List.eraseIdx r n) = List.take n r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.drop_eraseIdx_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma drop_eraseIdx_succ {I : Type} :
    (n : ℕ) → (r : List I) → (hn : n < r.length) →
    r[n] :: List.drop n (List.eraseIdx r n) = List.drop n r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.take_insert_gt
declarations.statement:
lemma take_insert_gt {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (n m : ℕ) → (h : n < m) → (r : List I) →
    List.take n (List.insertIdx r m i) = List.take n r

declarations.name: Physlib.List.take_insert_let
declarations.statement:
lemma take_insert_let {I : Type} (i : I) :
    (n m : ℕ) → (h : m ≤ n) → (r : List I) → (hm : m ≤ r.length) →
    (List.take (n + 1) (List.insertIdx r m i)).Perm (i :: List.take n r)

sections.text: ## Insertion sort with equal fields

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMin_lt_length_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortMin_lt_length_succ {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (i : α) (l : List α) :
    insertionSortMinPos r i l < (insertionSortDropMinPos r i l).length.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMinPosFin
declarations.doc:
Given a list `i :: l` the left-most minimal position `a` of `i :: l` wrt `r`
as an element of `Fin (insertionSortDropMinPos r i l).length.succ`.
declarations.statement:
def insertionSortMinPosFin {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] (i : α) (l : List α) :
    Fin (insertionSortDropMinPos r i l).length.succ

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMin_lt_mem_insertionSortDropMinPos
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortMin_lt_mem_insertionSortDropMinPos {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) (l : List α)
    (i : Fin (insertionSortDropMinPos r a l).length) :
    r (insertionSortMin r a l) ((insertionSortDropMinPos r a l)[i])

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMinPos_insertionSortEquiv
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortMinPos_insertionSortEquiv {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (a : α) (l : List α) :
    insertionSortEquiv r (a ::l) (insertionSortMinPos r a l) =
    ⟨0, by simp [List.orderedInsert_length]⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_gt_zero_of_ne_insertionSortMinPos
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_gt_zero_of_ne_insertionSortMinPos {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop)
    [DecidableRel r] (a : α) (l : List α) (k : Fin (a :: l).length)
    (hk : k ≠ insertionSortMinPos r a l) :
    ⟨0, by simp [List.orderedInsert_length]⟩ < insertionSortEquiv r (a :: l) k

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortMin_lt_mem_insertionSortDropMinPos_of_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortMin_lt_mem_insertionSortDropMinPos_of_lt {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop)
    [DecidableRel r] (a : α) (l : List α)
    (i : Fin (insertionSortDropMinPos r a l).length)
    (h : (insertionSortMinPosFin r a l).succAbove i < insertionSortMinPosFin r a l) :
    ¬ r ((insertionSortDropMinPos r a l)[i]) (insertionSortMin r a l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_insertionSort
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_insertionSort {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (l1 : List α) :
    List.insertionSort r (List.insertionSort r l1) = List.insertionSort r l1

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_commute {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a b : α) (hr : ¬ r a b) : (l : List α) →
    List.orderedInsert r a (List.orderedInsert r b l) =
      List.orderedInsert r b (List.orderedInsert r a l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_orderedInsert_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_orderedInsert_append {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) : (l1 l2 : List α) →
    List.insertionSort r (List.orderedInsert r a l1 ++ l2) = List.insertionSort r (a :: l1 ++ l2)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_insertionSort_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_insertionSort_append {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] : (l1 l2 : List α) →
    List.insertionSort r (List.insertionSort r l1 ++ l2) = List.insertionSort r (l1 ++ l2)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_append_insertionSort_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_append_insertionSort_append {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] : (l1 l2 l3 : List α) →
    List.insertionSort r (l1 ++ List.insertionSort r l2 ++ l3) =
      List.insertionSort r (l1 ++ l2 ++ l3)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_length
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_length {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] (a : α) (l : List α) :
    (List.orderedInsert r a l).length = (a :: l).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_orderedInsert
declarations.statement:
lemma takeWhile_orderedInsert {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r]
    (a b : α) (hr : ¬ r a b) : (l : List α) →
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r a c)) (List.orderedInsert r b l)).length =
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r a c)) l).length + 1

declarations.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_orderedInsert'
declarations.statement:
lemma takeWhile_orderedInsert' {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r]
    (a b : α) (hr : ¬ r a b) : (l : List α) →
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r b c)) (List.orderedInsert r a l)).length =
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => !decide (r b c)) l).length

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_cons_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_cons_succ {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (a : α) (l : List α) (n : ℕ) (hn : n + 1 < (a :: l).length) :
    insertionSortEquiv r (a :: l) ⟨n + 1, hn⟩ =
    Fin.cast (by simp)
      ((Fin.succAbove ⟨orderedInsertPos r (List.insertionSort r l) a,
          orderedInsertPos_lt_length r (List.insertionSort r l) a⟩)
        (insertionSortEquiv r l ⟨n, by simpa using hn⟩))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_commute {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a b : α) (hr : ¬ r a b) (n : ℕ) : (l : List α) →
    (hn : n + 2 < (a :: b :: l).length) →
    insertionSortEquiv r (a :: b :: l) ⟨n + 2, hn⟩ = (finCongr (by simp))
    (insertionSortEquiv r (b :: a :: l) ⟨n + 2, hn⟩)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_orderedInsert_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_orderedInsert_append {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a a2 : α) : (l1 l2 : List α) →
    (insertionSortEquiv r (List.orderedInsert r a l1 ++ a2 :: l2) ⟨l1.length + 1, by
      simp⟩)
    = (finCongr (by
      simp only [List.cons_append, List.insertionSort_cons, orderedInsert_length, List.length_cons,
        List.length_insertionSort, List.length_append]
      omega))
      ((insertionSortEquiv r (a :: l1 ++ a2 :: l2)) ⟨l1.length + 1, by simp⟩)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSortEquiv_insertionSort_append
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSortEquiv_insertionSort_append {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) : (l1 l2 : List α) →
    (insertionSortEquiv r (List.insertionSort r l1 ++ a :: l2) ⟨l1.length, by simp⟩)
    = finCongr (by simp) (insertionSortEquiv r (l1 ++ a :: l2) ⟨l1.length, by simp⟩)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_filter_of_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_filter_of_pos {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [IsTrans α r] (a : α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : p a) : (l : List α) →
    (hl : l.Pairwise r) →
    List.filter p (List.orderedInsert r a l) = List.orderedInsert r a (List.filter p l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.orderedInsert_filter_of_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma orderedInsert_filter_of_neg {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    (a : α) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (h : ¬ p a) (l : List α) :
    List.filter p (List.orderedInsert r a l) = (List.filter p l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_filter
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_filter {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r] [Std.Total r]
    [IsTrans α r] (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p] : (l : List α) →
    List.insertionSort r (List.filter p l) =
    List.filter p (List.insertionSort r l)

declarations.name: Physlib.List.takeWhile_sorted_eq_filter
declarations.statement:
lemma takeWhile_sorted_eq_filter {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [IsTrans α r] (a : α) : (l : List α) → (hl : l.Pairwise r) →
    List.takeWhile (fun c => ¬ r a c) l = List.filter (fun c => ¬ r a c) l

declarations.name: Physlib.List.dropWhile_sorted_eq_filter
declarations.statement:
lemma dropWhile_sorted_eq_filter {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [IsTrans α r] (a : α) : (l : List α) → (hl : l.Pairwise r) →
    List.dropWhile (fun c => ¬ r a c) l = List.filter (fun c => r a c) l

declarations.name: Physlib.List.dropWhile_sorted_eq_filter_filter
declarations.statement:
lemma dropWhile_sorted_eq_filter_filter {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [IsTrans α r] (a : α) :(l : List α) → (hl : l.Pairwise r) →
    List.filter (fun c => r a c) l =
    List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l ++ List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ ¬ r c a) l

declarations.name: Physlib.List.filter_rel_eq_insertionSort
declarations.statement:
lemma filter_rel_eq_insertionSort {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) : (l : List α) →
    List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) (l.insertionSort r) =
    List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_of_eq_list
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_of_eq_list {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) (l1 l l2 : List α)
    (h : ∀ b ∈ l, r a b ∧ r b a) :
    List.insertionSort r (l1 ++ l ++ l2) =
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => ¬ r a c) ((l1 ++ l2).insertionSort r))
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l1)
    ++ l
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l2)
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ ¬ r c a) ((l1 ++ l2).insertionSort r))

declarations.name: Physlib.List.insertionSort_of_takeWhile_filter
declarations.statement:
lemma insertionSort_of_takeWhile_filter {α : Type} (r : α → α → Prop) [DecidableRel r]
    [Std.Total r] [IsTrans α r] (a : α) (l1 l2 : List α) :
    List.insertionSort r (l1 ++ l2) =
    (List.takeWhile (fun c => ¬ r a c) ((l1 ++ l2).insertionSort r))
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l1)
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ r c a) l2)
    ++ (List.filter (fun c => r a c ∧ ¬ r c a) ((l1 ++ l2).insertionSort r))

modules.title: One-parameter subgroups of real Banach algebras
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Let `E` be a real Banach algebra. This file proves that every continuous additive character
`U : AddChar ℝ E` has the form `U(t) = exp (t • A)`, where `A = deriv U 0`.

This is the Banach-algebra argument underlying the correspondence between norm-continuous unitary
one-parameter groups and bounded self-adjoint generators. See
`Physlib.Mathematics.ForMathlib.OneParameterSubgroups.Unitary` for that correspondence.

**Proof outline.** Continuity at zero implies that, for sufficiently small `d > 0`, the integral of
`U` over `[0, d]` is close to `d • 1` and therefore invertible. If `I` is the indefinite integral of
`U`, the homomorphism law gives `U(t) * I(d) = I(t + d) - I(t)`. This identity proves that `U` is
differentiable. Setting `A` to the derivative at zero then gives the differential equation
`U'(t) = U(t)A`. Consequently `U(t) * exp (-tA)` has zero derivative and is constant. Uniqueness
follows by differentiating two exponential representations at zero.

## ii. Key results

* `OneParameterSubgroup.apply_eq_exp_smul_deriv`: A continuous one-parameter subgroup is the
  exponential of its derivative at zero.
* `OneParameterSubgroup.generator_unique`: Any exponential generator equals the derivative at zero.

## iii. References

* None.

declarations.doc:
`NormedSpace.exp`'s API wants a `ℚ`-algebra structure (for the `1/n!` coefficients), which
isn't automatic from `NormedAlgebra ℝ E` alone; derive it once here rather than at each use site.

    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, U t = NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) : A = deriv U 0

modules.title: Unitary one-parameter groups
modules.doc:
A norm-continuous unitary one-parameter group on a complex Hilbert space has a unique bounded
self-adjoint generator. With the convention used here, the group generated by `A` is
`U(t) = exp (-itA)`.

The same correspondence describes bounded generators of time translations, spatial translations,
rotations, and other norm-continuous unitary one-parameter groups. The general theorem for strongly
continuous groups and unbounded generators requires spectral theory that is not yet available in
Physlib.

## Main results

* `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator`: The canonical bounded self-adjoint generator.
* `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.apply_eq_exp_generator`: The formula `U(t) = exp (-itA)`.
* `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint`: The group generated by a bounded self-adjoint operator.
* `UnitaryOneParameterGroup.stoneEquiv`: Stone's correspondence for bounded generators.

## References

* M. H. Stone, Linear Transformations in Hilbert Space III. Operational Methods and Group Theory,
  Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. 16 (1930), 172-175. [ref: stone_1930]

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup
declarations.doc: A norm-continuous unitary one-parameter group on a complex Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
structure UnitaryOneParameterGroup (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    [CompleteSpace H] where
  /-- The additive character from the real parameter to unitary operators. -/
  toAddChar : AddChar ℝ (H →L[ℂ] H)
  /-- The group is valued in the unitary operators on `H`. -/
  mem_unitary : ∀ t, toAddChar t ∈ unitary (H →L[ℂ] H)
  /-- The group is continuous in the operator norm. -/
  continuous : Continuous toAddChar
instance : CoeFun (UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) fun _ => ℝ → (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {U V : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H} (h : ∀ t, U t = V t) : U = V

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.apply_eq_exp_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_exp_deriv (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    U t = NormedSpace.exp ((t : ℂ) • deriv U 0)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.adjoint_eq
declarations.statement: lemma adjoint_eq (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) : (U t).adjoint = U (-t)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator
declarations.doc: The bounded self-adjoint generator of `U`, in the convention `U(t) = exp (-itA)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.apply_eq_exp_generator
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_exp_generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    U t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • U.generator)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_unique
declarations.doc:
Any exponential generator of a unitary one-parameter group equals `U.generator`; the
uniqueness of the derivative at zero (`OneParameterSubgroup.generator_unique`) is the underlying
fact, restated here in terms of the physics convention.
declarations.statement:
lemma generator_unique (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (A : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (h : ∀ t : ℝ, U t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • A)) :
    A = U.generator

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.adjoint_deriv_eq_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_deriv_eq_neg (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) :
    (deriv U 0).adjoint = -deriv U 0

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: The generator of a unitary one-parameter group is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement: lemma generator_isSelfAdjoint (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) : IsSelfAdjoint U.generator

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.commute_generator
declarations.doc: The generator commutes with every member of its one-parameter group.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    Commute U.generator (U t)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hasDerivAt
declarations.doc: The derivative of a unitary one-parameter group in terms of its self-adjoint generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt U (U t * (-(Complex.I • U.generator))) t

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.hasDerivAt_star
declarations.doc: The derivative of the adjoint unitary path.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_star (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => star (U s)) (star (U t) * (Complex.I • U.generator)) t

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: The unitary one-parameter group generated by a bounded self-adjoint operator.
declarations.statement:
def ofSelfAdjoint {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    UnitaryOneParameterGroup H

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSelfAdjoint_apply {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (t : ℝ) :
    ofSelfAdjoint hA t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I) • A)

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.ofSelfAdjoint_generator
declarations.doc:
`ofSelfAdjoint` recovers `U` from its own generator: this is the defining property used to
show `stoneEquiv` is a left inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSelfAdjoint_generator (U : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H) :
    ofSelfAdjoint U.generator_isSelfAdjoint = U

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.generator_ofSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
The generator of `ofSelfAdjoint hA` is `A` itself: this is the defining property used to show
`stoneEquiv` is a right inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma generator_ofSelfAdjoint {A : H →L[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    (ofSelfAdjoint hA).generator = A

declarations.name: UnitaryOneParameterGroup.stoneEquiv
declarations.doc:
Stone's correspondence between norm-continuous unitary one-parameter groups and bounded
self-adjoint generators.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stoneEquiv :
    UnitaryOneParameterGroup H ≃ {A : H →L[ℂ] H // IsSelfAdjoint A}

modules.title: Orthogonal matrices and the dot product
modules.doc:
An orthogonal matrix — a square matrix `A` with `Aᵀ A = 1` — preserves the dot product of vectors,
and in particular their squared lengths. This is the algebraic content behind the
frame-independence of the *rotational* kinetic energy in rigid-body dynamics: rotating a velocity
does not change its speed.

declarations.name: Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
An orthogonal matrix preserves the dot product: if `Aᵀ A = 1` then `(A v) ⬝ᵥ (A w) = v ⬝ᵥ w`.
Taking `w = v` shows orthogonal matrices preserve squared lengths, `(A v) ⬝ᵥ (A v) = v ⬝ᵥ v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma dotProduct_mulVec_orthogonal {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {n : Type*} [Fintype n]
    [DecidableEq n] {A : Matrix n n R} (hA : Aᵀ * A = 1) (v w : n → R) :
    (A *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ w) = v ⬝ᵥ w

modules.title: Schur triangulation
modules.doc:
Schur triangulation is more commonly known as Schur decomposition or Schur triangularization, but
"triangulation" makes the API more readable. It states that a square matrix over an algebraically
closed field, e.g., `ℂ`, is unitarily similar to an upper triangular matrix.

## Main definitions

- `Matrix.schur_triangulation` : a matrix `A : Matrix n n 𝕜` with `𝕜` being algebraically closed can
be decomposed as `A = U * T * star U` where `U` is unitary and `T` is upper triangular.
- `Matrix.schurTriangulationUnitary` : the unitary matrix `U` as previously stated.
- `Matrix.schurTriangulation` : the upper triangular matrix `T` as previously stated.
- Some auxiliary definitions are not meant to be used directly, but
`LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux.of` contains the main algorithm for the triangulation procedure.

sections.text:
## Schur's recursive triangulation procedure

Given a linear endomorphism `f` on a non-trivial finite-dimensional vector space `E` over an
algebraically closed field `𝕜`, one can always pick an eigenvalue `μ` of `f` whose corresponding
eigenspace `V` is non-trivial. Given that `E` is also an inner product space, let `bV` and `bW` be
orthonormal bases for `V` and `Vᗮ` respectively. Then, the collection of vectors in `bV` and `bW`
forms an orthonormal basis `bE` for `E`, as the direct sum of `V` and `Vᗮ` is an internal
decomposition of `E`. The matrix representation of `f` with respect to `bE` satisfies
$$
\sideset{_\mathrm{bE}}{_\mathrm{bE}}{[f]} =
\begin{bmatrix}
  \sideset{_\mathrm{bV}}{_\mathrm{bV}}{[f]} &
  \sideset{_\mathrm{bW}}{_\mathrm{bV}}{[f]} \\
  \sideset{_\mathrm{bV}}{_\mathrm{bW}}{[f]} &
  \sideset{_\mathrm{bW}}{_\mathrm{bW}}{[f]}
\end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix} \mu I & □ \\ 0 & \sideset{_\mathrm{bW}}{_\mathrm{bW}}{[f]} \end{bmatrix},
$$
which is upper triangular as long as $\sideset{_\mathrm{bW}}{_\mathrm{bW}}{[f]}$ is. Finally, one
observes that the recursion from $\sideset{_\mathrm{bE}}{_\mathrm{bE}}{[f]}$ to
$\sideset{_\mathrm{bW}}{_\mathrm{bW}}{[f]}$ is well-founded, as the dimension of `bW` is smaller
than that of `bE` because `bV` is non-trivial.

However, in order to leverage `DirectSum.IsInternal.collectedOrthonormalBasis`, the type
`Σ b, cond b (Fin m) (Fin n)` has to be used instead of the more natural `Fin m ⊕ Fin n` while their
equivalence is propositionally established by `Equiv.sumEquivSigmalCond`.

declarations.name: Fin.subNat'
declarations.doc: `subNat' i h` subtracts `m` from `i`. This is an alternative form of `Fin.subNat`.
declarations.statement: def Fin.subNat' (i : Fin (m + n)) (h : ¬ i < m) : Fin n

declarations.name: Equiv.sumEquivSigmalCond
declarations.doc: An alternative form of `Equiv.sumEquivSigmaBool` where `Bool.casesOn` is replaced by `cond`.
declarations.statement: def sumEquivSigmalCond : Fin m ⊕ Fin n ≃ Σ b, cond b (Fin m) (Fin n)

declarations.name: Equiv.finAddEquivSigmaCond
declarations.doc:
The composition of `finSumFinEquiv` and `Equiv.sumEquivSigmalCond` used by
`LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux.of`.
declarations.statement: def finAddEquivSigmaCond : Fin (m + n) ≃ Σ b, cond b (Fin m) (Fin n)

declarations.name: Equiv.finAddEquivSigmaCond_true
declarations.statement: lemma finAddEquivSigmaCond_true (h : i < m) : finAddEquivSigmaCond i = ⟨true, i, h⟩

declarations.statement: lemma finAddEquivSigmaCond_false (h : ¬ i < m) : finAddEquivSigmaCond i = ⟨false, i.subNat' h⟩

declarations.doc: The type family parameterized by `Bool` is finite if each type variant is finite.
declarations.statement: instance [M : Fintype m] [N : Fintype n] (b : Bool) : Fintype (cond b m n)

declarations.name: Matrix.UpperTriangular
declarations.doc: The subtype of upper triangular matrices.
declarations.statement: abbrev UpperTriangular (n R) [LT n] [CommRing R]

declarations.name: LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux
declarations.doc:
**Don't use this definition directly.** Instead, use `Matrix.schurTriangulationBasis`,
`Matrix.schurTriangulationUnitary`, and `Matrix.schurTriangulation`. See also
`LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux.of` and `Matrix.schurTriangulationAux`.
declarations.statement:
structure SchurTriangulationAux (f : Module.End 𝕜 E) where
  /-- The dimension of the inner product space `E`. -/
  dim : ℕ
  hdim : Module.finrank 𝕜 E = dim
  /-- An orthonormal basis of `E` that induces an upper triangular form for `f`. -/
  basis : OrthonormalBasis (Fin dim) 𝕜 E
  upperTriangular : (toMatrix basis.toBasis basis.toBasis f).IsUpperTriangular

declarations.name: LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux.of
declarations.doc:
**Don't use this definition directly.** This is the key algorithm behind
`Matrix.schur_triangulation`.
declarations.statement:
protected noncomputable def SchurTriangulationAux.of
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] (f : Module.End 𝕜 E) :
    SchurTriangulationAux f

declarations.name: Matrix.schurTriangulationAux
declarations.doc:
This is `LinearMap.SchurTriangulationAux` adapted for matrices in the
Euclidean space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def schurTriangulationAux :
    OrthonormalBasis n 𝕜 (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n) × UpperTriangular n 𝕜

declarations.name: Matrix.schurTriangulationBasis
declarations.doc:
The change of basis that induces the upper triangular form `A.schurTriangulation` of a matrix
`A` over an algebraically closed field.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schurTriangulationBasis : OrthonormalBasis n 𝕜 (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)

declarations.name: Matrix.schurTriangulationUnitary
declarations.doc:
The unitary matrix that induces the upper triangular form `A.schurTriangulation` to which a
matrix `A` over an algebraically closed field is unitarily similar.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schurTriangulationUnitary : unitaryGroup n 𝕜

declarations.name: Matrix.schurTriangulation
declarations.doc:
The upper triangular form induced by `A.schurTriangulationUnitary` to which a matrix `A` over an
algebraically closed field is unitarily similar.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schurTriangulation : UpperTriangular n 𝕜

declarations.name: Matrix.schur_triangulation
declarations.doc:
**Schur triangulation**, **Schur decomposition** for matrices over an algebraically closed
field. In particular, a complex matrix can be converted to upper-triangular form by a change of
basis. In other words, any complex matrix is unitarily similar to an upper triangular matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma schur_triangulation :
    A = A.schurTriangulationUnitary * A.schurTriangulation * star A.schurTriangulationUnitary

modules.title: Positive-definite sesquilinear forms
modules.doc:
A sesquilinear form is positive-definite when it is symmetric and strictly positive on nonzero
vectors.

## i. Overview

Mathlib has positive-semidefinite sesquilinear forms (`LinearMap.IsPosSemidef`) and
positive-definite matrices (`Matrix.PosDef`), but no positive-definite sesquilinear forms.
`LinearMap.IsPosDef` fills this gap with the shape of `LinearMap.IsPosSemidef`: a structure
extending `LinearMap.IsSymm`. For a form `M →ₗ⋆[R] M →ₗ[R] R` symmetry is Hermiticity,
`star (B x y) = B y x`. A positive-definite form is positive-semidefinite and nondegenerate, and
in a basis it is positive-definite exactly when its matrix is.

## ii. Key results

- `LinearMap.IsPosDef` : a sesquilinear form is symmetric and `0 < B x x` for `x ≠ 0`.
- `LinearMap.IsPosDef.isPosSemidef` : a positive-definite form is positive-semidefinite.
- `LinearMap.IsPosDef.nondegenerate` : a positive-definite form is nondegenerate.
- `LinearMap.isPosDef_iff_posDef_toMatrix` : a form is positive-definite exactly when its matrix in
  a basis is.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Positive-definite sesquilinear forms
  - A.1. The definition
  - A.2. Consequences over a preorder
  - A.3. The matrix of a positive-definite form

## iv. References

- `LinearMap.IsPosSemidef` and `LinearMap.IsSymm`, in
  `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/SesquilinearForm/Basic.lean`;
- `Matrix.PosDef`, in `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean`.

sections.text:
## A. Positive-definite sesquilinear forms

### A.1. The definition
### A.2. Consequences over a preorder
### A.3. The matrix of a positive-definite form

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef
declarations.doc:
A sesquilinear form `B` is **positive-definite** if it is symmetric and `0 < B x x` for every
nonzero `x`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsPosDef [LT R] (B : M →ₛₗ[I₁] M →ₗ[R] R) : Prop extends isSymm : B.IsSymm where
  /-- `B` is strictly positive on nonzero vectors. -/
  pos : ∀ x, x ≠ 0 → 0 < B x x

declarations.name: LinearMap.isPosDef_def
declarations.statement:
lemma isPosDef_def [LT R] {B : M →ₛₗ[I₁] M →ₗ[R] R} :
    B.IsPosDef ↔ B.IsSymm ∧ ∀ x, x ≠ 0 → 0 < B x x

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef.isPosSemidef
declarations.doc: A positive-definite form is positive-semidefinite.
declarations.statement: lemma IsPosDef.isPosSemidef (hB : B.IsPosDef) : B.IsPosSemidef

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsPosDef.nondegenerate
declarations.doc: A positive-definite form is nondegenerate: a nonzero `x` is not orthogonal to itself.
declarations.statement: lemma IsPosDef.nondegenerate (hB : B.IsPosDef) : B.Nondegenerate

declarations.doc: A sesquilinear form is positive-definite exactly when its matrix in a basis is.

modules.title: Strict bounds on the square of the sine
modules.doc:
This file may eventually be upstreamed to Mathlib.

## i. Overview

Mathlib bounds the square of the sine by `sin x ^ 2 ≤ 1` for every real `x` (`Real.sin_sq_le_one`),
with equality exactly at the odd multiples of `π / 2`. This file records the strict form of that
bound, `sin x ^ 2 < 1` on the open interval `|x| < π / 2`, where the cosine is positive and
`1 - sin² x = cos² x`, together with its half-angle form `sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1` for `|θ| < π`.

Physlib uses the half-angle form for the simple pendulum: the parameter `sin² (θ₀ / 2)` of the
period formula lies in the domain `m < 1` of the complete elliptic integral `Real.completeEllipticK`
for every libration amplitude `|θ₀| < π`.

## ii. Key results

- `Real.sin_sq_lt_one` : `sin x ^ 2 < 1` for `|x| < π / 2`.
- `Real.sin_half_sq_lt_one` : `sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1` for `|θ| < π`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Strict bounds on the square of the sine

## iv. References

* Landau & Lifshitz, Mechanics, 3rd ed., §11, Problem 1 (the pendulum period, whose parameter is
  `sin² (θ₀ / 2)`). [ref: landau_mechanics]

sections.text:
## A. Strict bounds on the square of the sine

On `|x| < π / 2` the cosine is positive, so `1 - sin² x = cos² x` is positive; the half-angle form
follows by applying this at `x = θ / 2`.

declarations.name: Real.sin_sq_lt_one
declarations.doc: `sin x ^ 2 < 1` for `|x| < π / 2`: the cosine is positive there, and `1 - sin² x = cos² x`.
declarations.statement: lemma sin_sq_lt_one {x : ℝ} (h : |x| < π / 2) : sin x ^ 2 < 1

declarations.name: Real.sin_half_sq_lt_one
declarations.doc:
The half-angle form of `sin_sq_lt_one`: `sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1` for `|θ| < π`. For the pendulum
this says that the parameter `sin² (θ₀ / 2)` of the period formula lies in the domain of
`completeEllipticK` for every libration amplitude `|θ₀| < π`.
declarations.statement: lemma sin_half_sq_lt_one {θ : ℝ} (h : |θ| < π) : sin (θ / 2) ^ 2 < 1

modules.title: Properties of Tanh
modules.doc:
We want to prove that the reflectionless potential is a Schwartz map.
This means proving that pointwise multiplication of a Schwartz map with tanh is a Schwartz map.
This means we need to prove that all derivatives of tanh are bounded and continuous, so that
the nth derivative of a function multiplied by tanh decays faster than any polynomial.

## TODO
- Add these to mathlib eventually
- Fill in the proofs for the properties of tanh

declarations.doc: The derivative of tanh(x) is 1 - tanh(x)^2
declarations.statement: lemma deriv_tanh : deriv Real.tanh = fun x => 1 - Real.tanh x ^ 2

declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_tanh {n : ℕ} : ContDiff ℝ n tanh

declarations.statement: lemma tendsto_tanh_atTop : Filter.Tendsto Real.tanh Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_tanh_is_polynomial_of_tanh (n : ℕ) : ∃ P : Polynomial ℝ, ∀ x,
    iteratedDeriv n Real.tanh x = P.eval (Real.tanh x)

declarations.doc: For a polynomial P, show it's bounded on any bounded interval
declarations.statement:
lemma polynomial_bounded_on_interval (P : Polynomial ℝ) (a b : ℝ) :
    ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, x ∈ Set.Icc a b → |P.eval x| ≤ M

declarations.name: polynomial_tanh_bounded
declarations.doc: For a polynomial P, show that P (tanh x) is bounded on the real line
declarations.statement:
lemma polynomial_tanh_bounded (P : Polynomial ℝ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, |P.eval (Real.tanh x)| ≤ C

declarations.name: iteratedDeriv_tanh_bounded

modules.title: The adjoint representation of `SU(n)`
modules.doc:
The adjoint representation of `SU(n)` and its complexification, defined as `x ↦ g x g†`, and
the irreducibility of the latter.

## i. Overview

We define the adjont representation of `SU(n)` on its Lie algebra `su(n)` and its complexification.
The adjoint is defined by conjugation, `x ↦ g x g†`. It preserves the bracket, and its kernel is
the centre of `SU(n)`, the scalar matrices (A.1, A.2). On the underlying matrices of the
complexification the adjoint action of any unitary matrix, and in particular of any permutation of
the coordinates, is realised by an element of `SU(n)`; diagonal elements of `SU(n)` act on the
entries by phases (A.3). The complex adjoint representation is irreducible for `2 ≤ n` (C.1),
and hence, by Schur's lemma over an algebraically closed field, that every endomorphism of the
complexification commuting with the adjoint action is a multiple of the identity (C.2).

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.adjoint` : the adjoint representation on `su(n)`.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ` : the adjoint representation on the complexification.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjoint_eq_iff` : the adjoint representation is faithful modulo the centre.
- `SULieAlgebra.isIrreducible_adjointℂ` : the complex adjoint representation is irreducible.
- `SULieAlgebra.end_eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjointℂ` : Schur's lemma for the complex adjoint
  representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint representation
  - A.1. The real adjoint representation
  - A.2. The complex adjoint representation
  - A.3. The action on the underlying matrices
- B. The relation to single-entry elements
- C. Irreducibility and Schur's lemma
  - C.1. Irreducibility
  - C.2. Schur's lemma

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint
declarations.doc: The adjoint representation `x ↦ g x g†` of `SU(n)` on its real Lie algebra `su(n)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjoint {n : ℕ} :
    Representation ℝ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (SULieAlgebra n ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_val
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of `adjoint g x` is `g x g†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_val {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    (adjoint g x).1 = g.1 * x.1 * star g.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_lie
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation preserves the bracket, so `SU(n)` acts on `su(n)` by Lie algebra
automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_lie {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjoint g ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅adjoint g x, adjoint g y⁆

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_eq_one_iff
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the adjoint representation is the centre of `SU(n)`: `g` acts trivially exactly
when it is a scalar matrix `c 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_eq_one_iff {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjoint g = 1 ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Two elements of `SU(n)` have the same adjoint action exactly when they differ by a scalar:
the adjoint representation is faithful on `SU(n)` modulo its centre.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (g h : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjoint g = adjoint h ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • h.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation of `SU(n)` on the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`: the
complexification of the adjoint representation `adjoint` on `su(n)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointℂ {n : ℕ} :
    Representation ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (Complexification n)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂ_tmul {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (z : ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g (z ⊗ₜ x) = z ⊗ₜ adjoint g x

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_lie
declarations.doc:
The complex adjoint representation preserves the bracket of the complexification, so `SU(n)`
acts on `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` by Lie algebra automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂ_lie {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂ g ⁅A, B⁆ = ⁅adjointℂ g A, adjointℂ g B⁆

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_eq_one_iff
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the complex adjoint representation is the centre of `SU(n)`, as for the real
adjoint representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂ_eq_one_iff {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g = 1 ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
Two elements of `SU(n)` have the same complex adjoint action exactly when they differ by a
scalar, as for the real adjoint representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂ_eq_iff {n : ℕ} (g h : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointℂ g = adjointℂ h ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, g.1 = c • h.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ
declarations.doc: The adjoint representation conjugates the matrix, `M ↦ g M g†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ {n} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A : Complexification n) :
    toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) = g.1 * toMatrixℂ A * star g.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_eq_unitary
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by any unitary matrix is the adjoint action of an element of `SU(n)`: a
unitary matrix agrees with an element of `SU(n)` up to a phase, which conjugation does not
see.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_eq_unitary {n : ℕ} (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, ∀ A : Complexification n,
      toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) = U.1 * toMatrixℂ A * star U.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_perm
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action realises any permutation `σ` of the coordinates: some element of `SU(n)`
moves the entry `(x, y)` of every matrix to `(σ x, σ y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_perm {n : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, ∀ A x y,
      toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A) (σ x) (σ y) = toMatrixℂ A x y

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_apply_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of a diagonal element of `SU(n)` scales the entry at `(x, y)` of the
matrix by `d x * star (d y)`.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_trace
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_adjointℂ_trace {n} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (A : Complexification n) :
    (toMatrixℂ (adjointℂ g A)).trace = (toMatrixℂ A).trace

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_adjointℂ_singleℂ_eq_singleℂ
declarations.doc: All the off-diagonal matrix units `singleℂ` lie in one adjoint orbit
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_adjointℂ_singleℂ_eq_singleℂ {n : ℕ} {i j p q : Fin n} (hij : i ≠ j) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, adjointℂ g (singleℂ i j hij) = singleℂ p q hpq

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ
declarations.doc:
If the matrix of `A` has a non-zero entry at the off-diagonal position `(p, q)`, then
`singleℂ p q h` lies in the span of the adjoint orbit of `A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q)
    {A : Complexification n} (hA : toMatrixℂ A p q ≠ 0) :
    singleℂ p q h ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => adjointℂ g A)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_adjointℂ_eq_of_toMatrixℂ_eq_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of some element of `SU(n)` — the rotation by `π / 4` in the `(p, q)`-plane —
changes an element whose matrix is the diagonal matrix `d` only in the `(p, q)`-block, by
`(d p - d q) / 2` times `singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm - diagDiffℂ p q`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_adjointℂ_eq_of_toMatrixℂ_eq_diagonal {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q)
    {A : Complexification n} {d : Fin n → ℂ} (hA : toMatrixℂ A = diagonal d) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ, adjointℂ g A =
      A + ((d p - d q) / 2) • (singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm - diagDiffℂ p q)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_diagDiffℂ_eq_adjointℂ_singleℂ_add_singleℂ
declarations.doc:
The difference of two diagonal entries lies in the adjoint orbit of the sum of the two
elements supported at the corresponding off-diagonal entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_diagDiffℂ_eq_adjointℂ_singleℂ_add_singleℂ {n : ℕ} {p q : Fin n} (h : p ≠ q) :
    ∃ g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ,
      diagDiffℂ p q = adjointℂ g (singleℂ p q h + singleℂ q p h.symm)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ
declarations.doc:
The span of the adjoint orbit of a non-zero element contains an element supported at a single
off-diagonal entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_singleℂ_mem_span_range_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {A : Complexification n} (hA : A ≠ 0) :
    ∃ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q),
      singleℂ p q h ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => adjointℂ g A)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.isIrreducible_adjointℂ
declarations.doc: The complex adjoint representation of `SU(n)` is irreducible for `2 ≤ n`.
declarations.statement: lemma isIrreducible_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) : (adjointℂ (n := n)).IsIrreducible

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.end_eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjointℂ
declarations.doc: An endomorphism of the complexification commuting with the adjoint action is a scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma end_eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} {T : Module.End ℂ (Complexification n)}
    (hT : ∀ g, T ∘ₗ adjointℂ g = adjointℂ g ∘ₗ T) : ∃ μ : ℂ, T = μ • LinearMap.id

modules.title: The Lie algebra `su(n)` in the hermitian presentation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In physics, `su(n)` is described through generators `T^a`, `a = 1, …, n² - 1`, a basis of the
traceless hermitian `n × n` complex matrices, satisfying `[T^a, T^b] = i f_{abc} T^c` with real
structure constants `f_{abc}`. Here `i` is the imaginary unit and the repeated index `c` is summed.
This file makes the traceless hermitian matrices into a real Lie algebra with the bracket
`⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)`, on which the unitary group acts by conjugation. The construction allows
entries in any commutative `*`-ring `R` that is both a real and a complex `*`-algebra, as
`SULieAlgebra n R`; the Lie algebra `su(n)` itself is `SULieAlgebra n ℂ`.

Sending `z ⊗ x` to the matrix `z x` identifies the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` with the
traceless complex matrices. The inverse writes a traceless matrix `M` as `ℜ M + i ℑ M`, its real
and imaginary parts `ℜ M` and `ℑ M` being traceless hermitian.

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra n R` : traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices over `R`, as a real Lie algebra.
- `SULieAlgebra.conj` : the representation `x ↦ U x U†` of the unitary group.
- `SULieAlgebra.conj_lie` : conjugation by a unitary matrix preserves the bracket.
- `SULieAlgebra.Complexification n` : the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`.
- `SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ` : the underlying matrix of an element of the complexification.
- `SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_lie` : the matrix of a bracket is `i` times the commutator.
- `SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_injective`, `SULieAlgebra.range_toMatrixℂ` : the complexification is
  the traceless complex matrices.
- `SULieAlgebra.equivTraceKer` : the linear equivalence between the complexification and the
  traceless complex matrices.
- `SULieAlgebra.finrank_eq`, `SULieAlgebra.finrank_complexification` : `su(n)` and its
  complexification have dimension `n² - 1`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Traceless hermitian matrices
- B. The conjugation representation
- C. The bracket
- D. Conjugation preserves the bracket
- E. The complexification
  - E.1. The underlying matrix of the complexification
  - E.2. The element with a given traceless matrix
  - E.3. The injectivity and surjectivity of the matrix map
  - E.4. Commuting with all elements of `su(n)`
  - E.5. Linear equivalences
  - E.6. Specific elements
  - E.7. Spanning the complexification
- F. The dimension

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Traceless hermitian matrices

Since `i A` is skew-hermitian when `A` is hermitian, the traceless hermitian matrices form a real
vector space.

## B. The conjugation representation

Conjugation `x ↦ U x U†` by a unitary matrix `U` preserves traceless hermitian matrices, by
`U† U = 1` and cyclicity of the trace, and defines a representation of the unitary group.

## C. The bracket

From here on `R` is also a complex `*`-algebra, so that matrices can be multiplied by `i`. The
commutator of two hermitian matrices is skew-hermitian, and multiplying it by `i` makes it
hermitian again, giving the bracket `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)`. Being `i` times the commutator, it
is a Lie bracket.

Since `[i x, i y] = i ⁅x, y⁆`, multiplication by `i` turns this bracket into the commutator of
traceless skew-hermitian matrices, the usual mathematical presentation of `su(n)`.

The factor `i` flips the sign of the structure constants; if `[T^a, T^b] = i f_{abc} T^c`, then
`⁅T^a, T^b⁆ = -f_{abc} T^c`.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.ofMatrix
declarations.doc: The element given by a traceless hermitian matrix.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.val_ofMatrix
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of `ofMatrix A hA hT` is `A`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.star_val_eq
