declarations.statement: lemma star_val_eq (x : SULieAlgebra n R) : star x.1 = x.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.trace_val_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of an element is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_val_eq_zero (x : SULieAlgebra n R) : x.1.trace = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.conj
declarations.doc: The conjugation representation of the unitary group on `SULieAlgebra n R`: `x ↦ U x U†`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conj : Representation ℝ (unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (SULieAlgebra n R)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.val_conj_apply
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of `conj U x` is `U x U†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma val_conj_apply (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (x : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    (conj U x).1 = U.1 * x.1 * star U.1

declarations.doc: The bracket `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket (SULieAlgebra n R) (SULieAlgebra n R)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.val_bracket
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of `⁅x, y⁆` is `i (x y - y x)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma val_bracket (x y : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    ⁅x, y⁆.1 = Complex.I • (x.1 * y.1 - y.1 * x.1)

declarations.doc: `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)` makes `SULieAlgebra n R` a Lie ring.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : LieRing (SULieAlgebra n R)

declarations.doc: The bracket is `ℝ`-bilinear, so `SULieAlgebra n R` is a real Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : LieAlgebra ℝ (SULieAlgebra n R)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.conj_lie
declarations.doc:
Conjugation by a unitary matrix preserves the bracket, so `conj` acts by Lie algebra
automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_lie (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (x y : SULieAlgebra n R) :
    conj U ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅conj U x, conj U y⁆

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.Complexification
declarations.doc: The complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` of `su(n)`, a complex Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: abbrev Complexification (n : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of an element of the complexification, `z ⊗ x ↦ z x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toMatrixℂ : Complexification n →ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma toMatrixℂ_tmul (z : ℂ) (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) : toMatrixℂ (z ⊗ₜ x) = z • x.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.trace_toMatrixℂ
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of an element of the complexification is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_toMatrixℂ (A : Complexification n) : (toMatrixℂ A).trace = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_lie
declarations.doc:
The matrix of a bracket is `i` times the commutator of the matrices, `[A, B] ↦ i (A B - B A)`,
as in `su(n)` itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_lie (A B : Complexification n) :
    toMatrixℂ ⁅A, B⁆ = Complex.I • (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B - toMatrixℂ B * toMatrixℂ A)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ
declarations.doc: The element `1 ⊗ ℜ M + i ⊗ ℑ M` of the complexification with the traceless matrix `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofTracelessℂ (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    Complexification n

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_ofTracelessℂ
declarations.doc: The matrix of `ofTracelessℂ M` is `M = ℜ M + i ℑ M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_ofTracelessℂ (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    toMatrixℂ (ofTracelessℂ M hM) = M

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ_add
declarations.doc: `ofTracelessℂ` is additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTracelessℂ_add (M N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (hM : M.trace = 0) (hN : N.trace = 0)
    (hMN : (M + N).trace = 0) :
    ofTracelessℂ (M + N) hMN = ofTracelessℂ M hM + ofTracelessℂ N hN

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.ofTracelessℂ_toMatrixℂ
declarations.doc: An element of the complexification is recovered from its matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTracelessℂ_toMatrixℂ (A : Complexification n) :
    ofTracelessℂ (toMatrixℂ A) (trace_toMatrixℂ A) = A

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_injective
declarations.doc: An element of the complexification is determined by its matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma toMatrixℂ_injective : Function.Injective (toMatrixℂ (n := n))

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.range_toMatrixℂ
declarations.doc: The matrices of elements of the complexification are exactly the traceless matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma range_toMatrixℂ :
    LinearMap.range (toMatrixℂ (n := n)) = LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.commute_of_forall_commute_val
declarations.doc:
A matrix commuting with every element of `su(n)` commutes with every matrix: it commutes with
the traceless matrices, which `su(n)` spans over `ℂ`, and with the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_forall_commute_val {M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ}
    (h : ∀ x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ, Commute M x.1) (N : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) : Commute M N

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.equivTraceKer
declarations.doc:
The linear equivalence between the complexification of `su(n)` and the traceless complex
matrices, sending an element to its matrix.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def equivTraceKer :
    Complexification n ≃ₗ[ℂ] LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.val_equivTraceKer
declarations.doc: The matrix of `equivTraceKer A` is the matrix of `A`.
declarations.statement: lemma val_equivTraceKer (A : Complexification n) : (equivTraceKer A).1 = toMatrixℂ A

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_equivTraceKer_symm
declarations.doc: The matrix of `equivTraceKer.symm M` is `M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_equivTraceKer_symm (M : LinearMap.ker (traceLinearMap (Fin n) ℂ ℂ)) :
    toMatrixℂ (equivTraceKer.symm M) = M.1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ
declarations.doc: The element of the complexification supported at the single off-diagonal entry `(p, q)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def singleℂ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q) : Complexification n

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.diagDiffℂ
declarations.doc:
The element of the complexification corresponding to the difference of diagonal
entries `(p, p) - (q, q)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagDiffℂ (p q : Fin n) : Complexification n

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.submodule_eq_top_of_singleℂ_mem_of_diagDiffℂ_mem
declarations.doc:
A submodule of the complexification containing every element supported at a single
off-diagonal entry, and every difference of two diagonal entries, is everything.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.singleℂ_diagDiffℂ_span_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The elements supported at a single off-diagonal entry, together with the differences of two
diagonal entries, span the complexification.
declarations.statement:
lemma singleℂ_diagDiffℂ_span_eq_top {n : ℕ} :
    Submodule.span ℂ ({A : Complexification n | ∃ (p q : Fin n) (h : p ≠ q), A = singleℂ p q h} ∪
      {A : Complexification n | ∃ p q : Fin n, A = diagDiffℂ p q}) = ⊤

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.finrank_complexification
declarations.doc:
The complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` has complex dimension `n² - 1`: it is the traceless
matrices, and the trace is onto for `0 < n`.
declarations.statement: lemma finrank_complexification : Module.finrank ℂ (Complexification n) = n ^ 2 - 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.finrank_eq
declarations.doc: `su(n)` has real dimension `n² - 1`, the dimension of its complexification.
declarations.statement: lemma finrank_eq : Module.finrank ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ) = n ^ 2 - 1

modules.title: The contraction of adjoint indices of `SU(n)`
modules.doc:
The trace form on `su(n)` and on its complexification, and the invariant bilinear forms.

## i. Overview

The contraction `adjointContr` of two real adjoint indices is the trace form `x ⊗ y ↦ tr (x y)` on
`su(n)`, which is real since `x` and `y` are hermitian, and invariant under the adjoint action by
the cyclicity of the trace. It is symmetric, invariant under the bracket, and positive definite
since `tr (x x) = tr (x x†)` vanishes only for `x = 0` (A.1).

The contraction `adjointℂContr` of two complex adjoint indices is its complexification. On the
underlying matrices it is the trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)`, and it is again symmetric, invariant
under the bracket and nondegenerate (A.2).

Every bilinear form on the complexification is the contraction against an endomorphism, which
commutes with the adjoint action if the form is invariant. By Schur's lemma such an endomorphism is
a scalar, so every `SU(n)`-invariant bilinear form on the complexification is a multiple of the
contraction (B).

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.adjointContr` : the contraction of two real adjoint indices.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr` : the contraction of two complex adjoint indices.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_pos` : the real contraction is positive definite.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_nondegenerate` : the complex contraction is nondegenerate.
- `SULieAlgebra.intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr` : every intertwiner `adj ⊗ adj → ℂ` is a
  multiple of the complex contraction.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The contraction of adjoint indices
  - A.1. The real case
  - A.2. The complex case
- B. Invariant bilinear forms

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr
declarations.doc:
The contraction of two real adjoint indices: the trace form `x ⊗ y ↦ tr (x y)` on `su(n)`,
which is real since `x` and `y` are hermitian.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointContr {n : ℕ} : ((adjoint (n := n)).tprod adjoint).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℝ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℝ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_tmul
declarations.doc: The real contraction is the real part of the trace, `x ⊗ y ↦ re tr (x y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = (x.1 * y.1).trace.re

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation preserves the real contraction, so `SU(n)` acts on `su(n)` by
isometries.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_adjoint {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (adjoint g x ⊗ₜ adjoint g y) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.ofReal_adjointContr_tmul
declarations.doc: The trace `tr (x y)` of two elements of `su(n)` is real, equal to their contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofReal_adjointContr_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    (adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) : ℂ) = (x.1 * y.1).trace

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_symm {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = adjointContr (y ⊗ₜ x)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_lie
declarations.doc:
The real contraction is invariant under the bracket, `tr (⁅x, y⁆ z) = tr (x ⁅y, z⁆)`; in terms
of generators, the structure constants `tr (T^a ⁅T^b, T^c⁆)` are totally antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_lie {n : ℕ} (x y z : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (⁅x, y⁆ ⊗ₜ z) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ ⁅y, z⁆)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_nonneg
declarations.doc: The real contraction is positive semidefinite: `tr (x x) = tr (x x†) ≥ 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma adjointContr_self_nonneg {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) : 0 ≤ adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The real contraction of `x` with itself vanishes only for `x = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_self_eq_zero_iff {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x) = 0 ↔ x = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_self_pos
declarations.doc: The real contraction is positive definite, making it an inner product on `su(n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_self_pos {n : ℕ} {x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    0 < adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ x)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_separating_left
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_separating_left {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ)
    (hx : ∀ y, adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = 0) : x = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_separating_right
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_separating_right {n : ℕ} (y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ)
    (hy : ∀ x, adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = 0) : y = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_flip_injective
declarations.doc: The real contraction separates `su(n)`: `y ↦ (x ↦ re tr (x y))` is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_flip_injective {n : ℕ} :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).flip

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_isSymm
declarations.doc: The real contraction, as a bilinear form, is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_isSymm {n : ℕ} :
    LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: The real contraction, as a bilinear form, is nondegenerate.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_nondegenerate {n : ℕ} :
    (TensorProduct.curry (adjointContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).Nondegenerate

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr
declarations.doc:
The contraction of two complex adjoint indices: the complexification of the real contraction
`adjointContr`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointℂContr {n : ℕ} : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_adjointℂ
declarations.doc: The adjoint representation preserves the complex contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_adjointℂ {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (adjointℂ g A ⊗ₜ adjointℂ g B) = adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_tmul
declarations.doc: The contraction is the trace form, `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_tmul (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B).trace

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
On the real elements `1 ⊗ x` of the complexification the complex contraction is the real
contraction, so the two agree on real gauge fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_one_tmul {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointℂContr ((1 ⊗ₜ x) ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ y)) = adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_symm {n} (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = adjointℂContr (B ⊗ₜ A)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_lie
declarations.doc: The complex contraction is invariant under the bracket, `tr (⁅A, B⁆ C) = tr (A ⁅B, C⁆)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_lie {n} (A B C : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (⁅A, B⁆ ⊗ₜ C) = adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ ⁅B, C⁆)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_separating_left
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_separating_left {n} (A : Complexification n)
    (hA : ∀ B, adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = 0) : A = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_separating_right
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_separating_right {n} (B : Complexification n)
    (hB : ∀ A, adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = 0) : B = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_flip_injective
declarations.doc: The contraction separates the complexification: `B ↦ (A ↦ tr (A B))` is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_flip_injective :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).flip

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_isSymm
declarations.doc: The complex contraction, as a bilinear form, is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_isSymm {n : ℕ} :
    LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: The complex contraction, as a bilinear form, is nondegenerate.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_nondegenerate {n : ℕ} :
    (TensorProduct.curry (adjointℂContr (n := n)).toLinearMap).Nondegenerate

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.exists_eq_adjointℂContr_tmul
declarations.doc:
Every bilinear form on the complexification is the contraction against an endomorphism,
the contraction being nondegenerate.

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂ_comp_eq_of_adjointℂContr_tmul
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism representing an invariant bilinear form commutes with the adjoint
action.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂ_comp_eq_of_adjointℂContr_tmul {n : ℕ}
    (B : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
      (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ))
    {T : Module.End ℂ (Complexification n)} (hT : ∀ A C, B (A ⊗ₜ C) = adjointℂContr (T A ⊗ₜ C))
    (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    T ∘ₗ adjointℂ g = adjointℂ g ∘ₗ T

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr
declarations.doc:
Every intertwiner `adj ⊗ adj → ℂ` is a multiple of the contraction: up to scale, the
contraction is the unique `SU(n)`-invariant bilinear form on the complexification.
declarations.statement:
lemma intertwiningMap_eq_smul_adjointℂContr {n : ℕ}
    (B : ((adjointℂ (n := n)).tprod adjointℂ).IntertwiningMap
      (Representation.trivial ℂ (specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) ℂ)) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, B = z • adjointℂContr

modules.title: The adjoint action in the Gell-Mann basis
modules.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `SU(n)` on `su(n)` in the generalized Gell-Mann basis.

## i. Overview

The adjoint action `x ↦ g x g†` of `g ∈ SU(n)` on `su(n)` is, in the Gell-Mann basis, a real
matrix `R(g)` with entries `re tr (λ_i g λ_j g†) / 2`. As `g ↦ R(g)` is a monoid homomorphism and
the adjoint action preserves the contraction, `R(g)` is orthogonal (A). It acts on the Gell-Mann
matrices as `g λ_j g† = ∑ i, R_ij(g) λ_i`, and on the coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis by matrix
multiplication (B).

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis` : the matrix of the adjoint action in the Gell-Mann basis.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_transpose_mul_self` : that matrix is orthogonal.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjoint_gellMannMatrices` : the adjoint action on the Gell-Mann matrices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrix of the adjoint action
- B. The adjoint action on Gell-Mann matrices and coordinates

## iv. References

* https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GeneralizedGell-MannMatrix.html

sections.text: ## A. The matrix of the adjoint action
## B. The adjoint action on Gell-Mann matrices and coordinates

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `g` in the Gell-Mann basis, a real matrix, as a monoid
homomorphism from `SU(n)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointGellMannBasis {n : ℕ} :
    specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ →* Matrix (GellMannIndex n) (GellMannIndex n) ℝ

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of the matrix of the adjoint action, `re tr (λ_i g λ_j g†) / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_apply {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (i j : GellMannIndex n) : adjointGellMannBasis g i j =
      ((gellMannMatrices i).1 * (g.1 * (gellMannMatrices j).1 * star g.1)).trace.re / 2

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_inv
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of `g⁻¹` is the transpose of that of `g`, the adjoint action
preserving the contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_inv {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    adjointGellMannBasis g⁻¹ = (adjointGellMannBasis g)ᵀ

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointGellMannBasis_transpose_mul_self
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action is orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointGellMannBasis_transpose_mul_self {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    (adjointGellMannBasis g)ᵀ * adjointGellMannBasis g = 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrix_adjointℂ_gellMannBasisℂ
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the complex adjoint action in the complex Gell-Mann basis is the real matrix of
the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_adjointℂ_gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix gellMannBasisℂ gellMannBasisℂ (adjointℂ g) =
      (adjointGellMannBasis g).map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjoint_gellMannMatrices
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action on a Gell-Mann matrix is a combination of Gell-Mann matrices with
coefficients the entries of the matrix of the adjoint action,
`g λ_j g† = ∑ i, R_ij(g) λ_i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ) (j : GellMannIndex n) :
    adjoint g (gellMannMatrices j) = ∑ i, adjointGellMannBasis g i j • gellMannMatrices i

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_repr_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action on the coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis is multiplication by the matrix of
the adjoint action, `A^i ↦ R_ij(g) A^j`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannBasis_repr_adjoint {n : ℕ} (g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin n) ℂ)
    (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    gellMannBasis.repr (adjoint g x) = adjointGellMannBasis g *ᵥ gellMannBasis.repr x

modules.title: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices
modules.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices, orthogonality, the basis and the structure constants they form.

## i. Overview

The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the standard basis of `su(n)`, generalizing the Pauli
matrices (`n = 2`) and the Gell-Mann matrices (`n = 3`). They are labelled by `GellMannIndex n`,
which has `n² - 1` elements, of three kinds (A):

- for `p < q` the symmetric matrix `E_pq + E_qp`,
- for `p < q` the antisymmetric matrix `-i E_pq + i E_qp`,
- for `1 ≤ m ≤ n - 1` the diagonal matrix `√(2 / (m (m + 1))) (E_00 + ⋯ + E_(m-1)(m-1) - m E_mm)`.

They are orthogonal under the contraction, `adjointContr (λ_i ⊗ λ_j) = tr (λ_i λ_j) = 2 δ_ij`, and
so linearly independent (B).

As there are as many as the dimension `n² - 1` of `su(n)`, they form a basis, whose coordinates
are the contractions `adjointContr (λ_i ⊗ x) / 2`, and its base change is a basis of the
complexification (C). In this basis the bracket defines the structure constants
`[λ_a, λ_b] = 2 i f_abc λ_c`, which are totally antisymmetric (D).

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex` : the labels of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices` : the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices` : the Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal.
- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis` : the Gell-Mann basis of `su(n)`.
- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ` : the Gell-Mann basis of the complexification of `su(n)`.
- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst` : the structure constants, `[λ_a, λ_b] = 2 i f_abc λ_c`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The indexing type of the Gell-Mann matrices
  - A.1. The cardinality of `GellMannIndex`
- B. The generalized Gell-Mann matrices
  - B.1. Symmetry properties
  - B.2. Explicit forms
  - B.3. Orthogonality
    - B.3.1. Between different types
    - B.3.2. Between the same type
    - B.3.3. The full orthogonality relation
  - B.4. Linear independence
- C. The Gell-Mann basis
  - C.1. The basis of `su(n)`
  - C.2. The basis of the complexification
- D. The structure constants

## iv. References

* https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GeneralizedGell-MannMatrix.html

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex
declarations.doc: The indexing type of the Gell-Mann matrices.
declarations.statement:
inductive GellMannIndex (n : ℕ)
  | symm (p : Fin n) (q : Fin n) (h : p < q) : GellMannIndex n
  | antisymm (p : Fin n) (q : Fin n) (h : p < q) : GellMannIndex n
  | diag (l : Fin (n - 1)) : GellMannIndex n

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannIndex_card
declarations.doc:
There are `n² - 1` generalized Gell-Mann matrices: `n (n - 1) / 2` symmetric ones, as many
antisymmetric ones, and `n - 1` diagonal ones.
declarations.statement: lemma gellMannIndex_card {n : ℕ} : Fintype.card (GellMannIndex n) = n ^ 2 - 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices
declarations.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices, as elements of `su(n)`:

- for `p < q`, the symmetric matrix `E_pq + E_qp`,
- for `p < q`, the antisymmetric matrix `-i E_pq + i E_qp`,
- for `l : Fin (n - 1)`, with `m = l + 1`, the diagonal matrix
  `√(2 / (m (m + 1))) (E_00 + ⋯ + E_(m-1)(m-1) - m E_mm)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} : GellMannIndex n → SULieAlgebra n ℂ

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_symm_isSymm
declarations.doc: The symmetric generalized Gell-Mann matrices are symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_symm_isSymm {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    Matrix.IsSymm (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)).1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_antisymm_transpose
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric generalized Gell-Mann matrices are antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_antisymm_transpose {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1ᵀ = -(gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_diag_isDiag
declarations.doc: The diagonal generalized Gell-Mann matrices are diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_diag_isDiag {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    Matrix.IsDiag (gellMannMatrices (.diag l)).1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_symm_val_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_symm_val_eq {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)).1 = single p q 1 + single q p 1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_antisymm_val_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_antisymm_val_eq {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)).1 = single p q (-Complex.I) + single q p Complex.I

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_diag_val_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_diag_val_eq {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    (gellMannMatrices (.diag l)).1 = diagonal fun x => (√(2 / ((l.1 + 1) * (l.1 + 2))) : ℝ) *
      if x.1 ≤ l.1 then 1 else if x.1 = l.1 + 1 then -(l.1 + 1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_antisymm_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_antisymm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p' q' h')) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_diag_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_diag_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_symm_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_symm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p' q' h')) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_diag_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_diag_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_symm_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_symm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) (p q : Fin n)
    (h : p < q) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h)) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_antisymm_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_antisymm_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) (p q : Fin n)
    (h : p < q) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h)) = 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_symm_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.symm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.symm p' q' h')) =
      if p = p' ∧ q = q' then 2 else 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_antisymm_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (p q : Fin n) (h : p < q)
    (p' q' : Fin n) (h' : p' < q') :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p q h) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.antisymm p' q' h')) =
      if p = p' ∧ q = q' then 2 else 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_self
declarations.doc: The diagonal Gell-Mann matrices are normalized, `tr (λ_l λ_l) = 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_self {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l)) = 2

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices_diag_orthogonal {n : ℕ} (l l' : Fin (n - 1)) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices (.diag l) ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices (.diag l')) =
      if l = l' then 2 else 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_gellMannMatrices
declarations.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal under the trace pairing,
with normalization `tr (λ_i λ_j) = 2 δ_ij`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (i j : GellMannIndex n) :
    adjointContr (gellMannMatrices i ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices j) = if i = j then 2 else 0

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.linearIndependent_gellMannMatrices
declarations.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are linearly independent over `ℝ`, being orthogonal under
the contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIndependent_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} :
    LinearIndependent ℝ (gellMannMatrices (n := n))

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis of `su(n)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gellMannBasis {n : ℕ} : Module.Basis (GellMannIndex n) ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_apply
declarations.statement: lemma gellMannBasis_apply {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) : gellMannBasis i = gellMannMatrices i

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasis_repr_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are the contractions with the Gell-Mann matrices,
`x = ∑ (adjointContr (λ_i ⊗ x) / 2) λ_i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannBasis_repr_apply {n : ℕ} (x : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasis.repr x i = adjointContr (gellMannMatrices i ⊗ₜ x) / 2

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis `1 ⊗ λ_i` of the complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} : Module.Basis (GellMannIndex n) ℂ (Complexification n)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannBasisℂ_apply {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasisℂ i = 1 ⊗ₜ gellMannMatrices i

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.toMatrixℂ_gellMannBasisℂ
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrixℂ_gellMannBasisℂ {n : ℕ} (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    toMatrixℂ (gellMannBasisℂ i) = (gellMannMatrices i).1

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannBasisℂ_repr_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinates in the complex Gell-Mann basis are the contractions with the Gell-Mann
matrices, `A = ∑ (adjointℂContr (λ_i ⊗ A) / 2) λ_i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannBasisℂ_repr_apply {n : ℕ} (A : Complexification n) (i : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannBasisℂ.repr A i = adjointℂContr (gellMannBasisℂ i ⊗ₜ A) / 2

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst
declarations.doc:
The structure constants of `su(n)` in the Gell-Mann basis, with the physics normalisation
`[λ_a, λ_b] = 2 i ∑ c, f_abc λ_c`, read off by the contraction:
`f_abc = tr ([λ_a, λ_b] λ_c) / (4 i) = -(1 / 4) adjointContr (⁅λ_a, λ_b⁆ ⊗ λ_c)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gellMannStructureConst {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) : ℝ

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.lie_gellMannMatrices
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two Gell-Mann matrices in terms of the structure constants,
`⁅λ_a, λ_b⁆ = -2 ∑ c, f_abc λ_c`, the bracket `⁅x, y⁆ = i (x y - y x)` carrying a factor `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_gellMannMatrices {n : ℕ} (a b : GellMannIndex n) :
    ⁅gellMannMatrices a, gellMannMatrices b⁆ =
      ∑ c, (-2 * gellMannStructureConst a b c) • gellMannMatrices c

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst_swap
declarations.doc: The structure constants are antisymmetric in their first two indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannStructureConst_swap {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannStructureConst b a c = -gellMannStructureConst a b c

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannStructureConst_cycle
declarations.doc:
The structure constants are invariant under cyclic permutations of their indices, the
contraction being invariant under the bracket. With `gellMannStructureConst_swap`, they are
totally antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannStructureConst_cycle {n : ℕ} (a b c : GellMannIndex n) :
    gellMannStructureConst b c a = gellMannStructureConst a b c

modules.title: The Pauli and Gell-Mann matrices
modules.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices in the special cases `n = 2` and `n = 3`.

## i. Overview

For `n = 2` the generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the Pauli matrices `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃` (A), and for
`n = 3` they are the Gell-Mann matrices `λ₁, …, λ₈` (B). In each case an equivalence of
`GellMannIndex n` with `Fin (n² - 1)` puts the labels in the standard order.

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_two` : for `n = 2`, the Pauli matrices `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃`.
- `SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_three` : for `n = 3`, the Gell-Mann matrices `λ₁, …, λ₈`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The case `n = 2`
- B. The case `n = 3`

## iv. References

* https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GeneralizedGell-MannMatrix.html

sections.text: ## A. The case `n = 2`
## B. The case `n = 3`

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex.equivTwo
declarations.doc:
For `n = 2`, the labelling of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices as the Pauli matrices
`σ₁, σ₂, σ₃` (as `0, 1, 2`): the symmetric, antisymmetric and diagonal matrices.
declarations.statement: def GellMannIndex.equivTwo : GellMannIndex 2 ≃ Fin 3

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_two
declarations.doc:
For `n = 2` the generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the Pauli matrices `σ₁, σ₂, σ₃`, labelled
by `GellMannIndex.equivTwo`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrices_two (i : Fin 3) :
    (gellMannMatrices (GellMannIndex.equivTwo.symm i)).1 = PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.GellMannIndex.equivThree
declarations.doc:
For `n = 3`, the labelling of the Gell-Mann matrices in the standard order `λ₁, …, λ₈`
(as `0, …, 7`): `λ₁, λ₂, λ₃` are the symmetric, antisymmetric and diagonal matrices of the first
two coordinates, `λ₄, λ₅` the symmetric and antisymmetric ones of the coordinates `0, 2`,
`λ₆, λ₇` those of the coordinates `1, 2`, and `λ₈` the second diagonal matrix.
declarations.statement: def GellMannIndex.equivThree : GellMannIndex 3 ≃ Fin 8

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.gellMannMatrices_three
declarations.doc:
For `n = 3` the generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the Gell-Mann matrices `λ₁, …, λ₈`, labelled
in the standard order by `GellMannIndex.equivThree`.

modules.title: The Killing form of `su(n)`
modules.doc:
The Killing form of `su(n)` and its complexification, and its relation to the adjoint contraction.

## i. Overview

The Killing form `K(A, B) = tr (ad A ∘ ad B)` of the complexification is computed by transporting
`ad A ∘ ad B` to the matrices, where it is `M ↦ -[A, [B, M]]`, the sign coming from the factor `i`
in the bracket. Its trace is `-2n tr (A B)` (A).

The contractions `adjointℂContr` and `adjointContr` of adjoint indices are therefore `-1 / (2n)`
times the Killing forms of the complexification and of `su(n)` (B).

## ii. Key results

- `SULieAlgebra.killingForm_eq_trace` : the Killing form of the complexification is `-2n` times
  the trace form.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_eq_killingForm` : the complex contraction is `-1 / (2n)` times the
  Killing form.
- `SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_eq_killingForm` : the real contraction is `-1 / (2n)` times the
  Killing form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Killing form as a trace
- B. The contraction as the Killing form

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Killing form as a trace
## B. The contraction as the Killing form

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.killingForm_eq_trace
declarations.doc:
The Killing form of the complexification is the trace form of the matrices,
`K(A, B) = -2n tr (A B)`. The sign comes from the factor `i` in the bracket, which makes
`ad A ∘ ad B` the map `M ↦ -[A, [B, M]]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma killingForm_eq_trace {n : ℕ} (A B : Complexification n) :
    killingForm ℂ (Complexification n) A B = - (2 * n) * (toMatrixℂ A * toMatrixℂ B).trace

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointℂContr_eq_killingForm
declarations.doc:
The contraction is the Killing form on the complexified Lie
algebra, up to a factor of `-1/(2n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointℂContr_eq_killingForm {n : ℕ} (A B : Complexification n) :
    adjointℂContr (A ⊗ₜ B) = -(1 / (2 * (n : ℂ))) * killingForm ℂ (Complexification n) A B

declarations.name: SULieAlgebra.adjointContr_eq_killingForm
declarations.doc: The contraction is the Killing form on the Lie algebra, up to a factor of `-1/(2n)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointContr_eq_killingForm {n : ℕ} (x y : SULieAlgebra n ℂ) :
    adjointContr (x ⊗ₜ y) = -(1 / (2 * (n : ℝ))) * killingForm ℝ (SULieAlgebra n ℂ) x y

modules.title: Adjoint of a linear map
modules.doc:
This module defines the adjoint of a linear map `f : E → F` where
`E` and `F` carry the instances of `InnerProductSpace'` over a field `𝕜`.

This is a generalization of the usual adjoint defined on `InnerProductSpace` for
continuous linear maps.

declarations.name: HasAdjoint
declarations.doc:
Adjoint of a linear map `f` such that `∀ x y, ⟪adjoint 𝕜 f y, x⟫ = ⟪y, f x⟫`.

This computes adjoint of a linear map the same way as `ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint` but it is
defined over `InnerProductSpace'`, which is a generalization of `InnerProductSpace` that provides
instances for products and function types. These instances make it easier to perform computations
compared to using the standard `InnerProductSpace` class.
declarations.statement:
structure HasAdjoint (f : E → F) (f' : F → E) where
  adjoint_inner_left (x : E) (y : F) : ⟪f' y, x⟫ = ⟪y, f x⟫

declarations.name: adjoint
declarations.statement: def adjoint (f : E → F)

declarations.name: HasAdjoint.adjoint_inner_right
declarations.statement:
lemma HasAdjoint.adjoint_inner_right {f : E → F} (hf : HasAdjoint 𝕜 f f') :
    ⟪x, f' y⟫ = ⟪f x, y⟫

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.hasAdjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma ContinuousLinearMap.hasAdjoint [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] (f : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    HasAdjoint 𝕜 f (fun y => fromL2 𝕜 (((toL2 𝕜) ∘L f ∘L (fromL2 𝕜)).adjoint (toL2 𝕜 y)))

declarations.name: adjoint_eq_clm_adjoint
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_eq_clm_adjoint [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace F] (f : E →L[𝕜] F) :
    _root_.adjoint 𝕜 f = fromL2 𝕜 ∘L (toL2 𝕜 ∘L f ∘L fromL2 𝕜).adjoint ∘L (toL2 𝕜)

declarations.name: HasAdjoint.adjoint_apply_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma HasAdjoint.adjoint_apply_zero {f : E → F} {f' : F → E}
    (hf : HasAdjoint 𝕜 f f') : f' 0 = 0

HasAdjoint.congr_adj

declarations.name: hasAdjoint_zero
declarations.statement: lemma hasAdjoint_zero : HasAdjoint 𝕜 (fun _ : E => (0 : F)) (fun _ => 0)

HasAdjoint.prodMk

lemma HasAdjoint.snd {f : E → F×G} {f'} (hf : HasAdjoint 𝕜 f f') :

lemma HasAdjoint.neg {f : E → F} {f'} (hf : HasAdjoint 𝕜 f f') :

HasAdjoint.sub

modules.title: Inner product space
modules.doc:
In this module we define the type class `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which is a
generalization of `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E`, as it does not require the condition `‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫`
but instead the condition `∃ (c > 0) (d > 0), c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ ⟪x,x⟫ ≤ d • ‖x‖^2`.
Instead `E` is equipped with a L₂ norm `‖x‖₂` which satisfies `‖x‖₂ = √⟪x,x⟫`.

This allows us to define the inner product space structure on product types `E × F` and
pi types `ι → E`, which would otherwise not be possible due to the use of max norm on these types.

We define the following maps:

- `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E` which sets `‖x‖₂ = ‖x‖`.
- `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)` which uses the fact that the norm
  defined on `WithLp 2 E` is L₂ norm.

sections.text: ## B. Deriving the inner product structure on `WithLp 2 E` from `InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E`
## C. Basic properties of the inner product

declarations.name: Norm₂
declarations.doc:
L₂ norm on `E`.

In particular, on product types `X×Y` and pi types `ι → X` this class provides L₂ norm unlike `‖·‖`.
declarations.statement:
class Norm₂ (E : Type*) where
  norm₂ : E → ℝ

declarations.name: InnerProductSpace'
declarations.doc:
Effectively as `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E` but it does not requires that `‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫`. It is
only required that they are equivalent `∃ (c > 0) (d > 0), c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ ⟪x,x⟫ ≤ d • ‖x‖^2`. The main
purpose of this class is to provide inner product space structure on product types `ExF` and
pi types `ι → E` without using `WithLp` gadget.

If you want to access L₂ norm use `‖x‖₂ := √⟪x,x⟫`.

This class induces `InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)` which equips `‖·‖` on `X` with L₂ norm.
This is very useful when translating results from `InnerProductSpace` to `InnerProductSpace'`
together with `toL2 : E →L[𝕜] (WithLp 2 E)` and `fromL2 : (WithL2 2 E) →L[𝕜] E`.

In short we have these implications:
```
  InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E
  InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (WithLp 2 E)
```

The reason behind this type class is that with current mathlib design the requirement
`‖x‖^2 = ⟪x,x⟫` prevents us to give inner product space structure on product type `E×F` and pi
type `ι → E` as they are equipped with max norm. One has to work with `WithLp 2 (E×F)` and
`WithLp 2 (ι → E)`. This places quite a bit inconvenience on users in certain scenarios.
In particular, the main motivation behind this class is to make computations of `adjFDeriv` and
`gradient` easy.
declarations.statement:
class InnerProductSpace' (𝕜 : Type*) (E : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
    extends Norm₂ E where
  /-- Core inner product properties. -/
  core : InnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 E
  /-- The inner product induces the L₂ norm. -/
  norm₂_sq_eq_re_inner : ∀ x : E, ‖x‖₂ ^ 2 = re (core.inner x x)
  /-- Norm induced by inner product is topologically equivalent to the given norm on E. -/
  inner_top_equiv_norm : ∃ c d : ℝ,
    0 < c ∧ 0 < d ∧
    ∀ x : E, (c • ‖x‖^2 ≤ re (core.inner x x)) ∧ (re (core.inner x x) ≤ d • ‖x‖^2)
instance [inst : InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E] : InnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 E
instance [inst : InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E] : Inner 𝕜 E

instance {𝕜 : Type*} {E : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] :
    InnerProductSpace' 𝕜 E

modules.title: Gaussians in inner product spaces
modules.doc:
Gaussians and their products with real linear exponentials as Schwartz maps.

## i. Overview

In this module we define Gaussians as Schwartz maps in general inner product spaces.

The most general Gaussian constructed is `exp (-2⁻¹ * ‖B⁻¹ (x - x₀)‖ ^ 2)` (mean `x₀`
and covariance `BBᵀ`) as a Schwartz map `𝓢(E, 𝕜)`, where `B : D ≃L[ℝ] E` is a linear equivalence
of inner product spaces. This is accomplished by first constructing the Gaussian
`exp (-2⁻¹ * ‖x‖ ^ 2)` as a Schwartz map `𝓢(E, ℝ)` using explicit bounds on the derivatives
of `‖x‖ ^ 2 = innerSL ℝ x x` and limiting properties of the real exponential,
then composing with an invertible affine transformation.

The Gaussians are left unnormalized since the appropriate condition will depend on context and
whether `E` is finite- or infinite-dimensional. For example, the normalization conditions when
interpreted as a probability density function vs. as a quantum state require different pre-factors.

For some relevant Gaussian integrals see
`Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Gaussian/FourierTransform`.

## ii. Key results

- `gaussian 𝕜 B x₀` : Given a linear equivalence `B : D ≃L[ℝ] E` and mean `x₀ : E`,
    the Gaussian `exp (-2⁻¹ * ‖B⁻¹ (x - x₀)‖ ^ 2)` centered on `x₀` as a Schwartz map `𝓢(E, 𝕜)`.
- `gaussian₀ 𝕜 B` : Given a linear equivalence `B : D ≃L[ℝ] E` of inner product spaces,
    the Gaussian `exp (-2⁻¹ * ‖B⁻¹ x‖ ^ 2)` centered on the origin as a Schwartz map `𝓢(E, 𝕜)`.
- `stdGaussian E 𝕜` : The standard Gaussian `exp (-2⁻¹ * ‖x‖ ^ 2)` as a Schwartz map `𝓢(E, 𝕜)`.
- `exp_mul_gaussian` : Completing the square for multiplication by `exp ⟪v, x⟫`.
- `gaussianExpMul 𝕜 B x₀ v` : This product as a Schwartz map when `D` and `E` are complete.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Standard, real-valued
- B. General, RCLike-valued
- C. Multiplication by a real linear exponential

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Standard, real-valued
## B. General, RCLike-valued

## C. Multiplication by a real linear exponential

Completeness is assumed to use the adjoint of `B`. The exponential has a real exponent,
even when the Gaussian is complex-valued.

declarations.name: InnerProductSpace.exp_mul_gaussian
declarations.doc: Multiplication by a real linear exponential shifts and rescales a general Gaussian.
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_mul_gaussian (v : E) :
    (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x)) : 𝕜) * gaussian 𝕜 B x₀ x =
      (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x₀ + 2⁻¹ * ‖B.toContinuousLinearMap.adjoint v‖ ^ 2)) : 𝕜) *
        gaussian 𝕜 B (x₀ + B (B.toContinuousLinearMap.adjoint v)) x

declarations.name: InnerProductSpace.gaussianExpMul
declarations.doc:
The product of `gaussian 𝕜 B x₀` with the real exponential `exp ⟪v, x⟫`, as a Schwartz map.
It has center `x₀ + B (Bᵀ v)` and the same covariance, with scale factor
`exp (⟪v, x₀⟫ + 2⁻¹ * ‖Bᵀ v‖ ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def gaussianExpMul (v : E) : 𝓢(E, 𝕜)

declarations.name: InnerProductSpace.gaussianExpMul_apply
declarations.doc: Evaluation of the bundled product agrees with pointwise multiplication by the exponential.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussianExpMul_apply (v : E) :
    gaussianExpMul 𝕜 B x₀ v x = (ofReal (rexp (inner ℝ v x)) : 𝕜) * gaussian 𝕜 B x₀ x

modules.title: Kronecker delta
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This module defines the Kronecker delta `kroneckerDelta i j` (notation `δ[i,j]`), equal to
`1` when `i = j` and `0` otherwise, together with its behaviour under scalar multiplication,
symmetrization, and finite sums. It also defines the `generalizedKroneckerDelta`, the
determinant of a matrix of Kronecker deltas.

## ii. Key results

- `kroneckerDelta` : the Kronecker delta on a type with decidable equality.
- `generalizedKroneckerDelta` : the determinant form `det (δ[μᵢ, νⱼ])`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Kronecker delta
- B. Conditions for smul to vanish
- C. Symmetrization
- D. Sums
- E. The generalized Kronecker delta

## iv. References

* None.
